title: consolidation: repoint dependants' native blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines to the 'Superseded by' successor
body:
## What

When issue consolidation closes an original as not planned with `Superseded by #S`, rewrite its dependants' native `blockedBy` edges and their `Blocked by:` body lines to point at the live successor `#S`.

## Evidence (managed private repo, 2026-10-19)

- 36 open `status:blocked` issues had native `blockedBy` edges that pointed **only** at closed, not-planned originals. Each original carried a trusted `Superseded by #S` comment, and every `#S` was open.
- `dependency-supersession-lib.sh` (GH#34341) correctly keeps these dependants blocked by following the comment chain at read time, so dispatch is right.
- Every other reader still sees a dependant whose blockers are all closed. That includes GitHub's UI, queue-depth counters, and operators triaging "blocked but nothing blocks it". In this case it triggered a manual audit of 48 issues.
- The edges were fixed by hand by adding `blocked_by` to `#S` and editing the body line.

## How

- In the consolidation path (`pulse-merge-duplicate-consolidation.sh` and the consolidation dispatcher), after posting `Superseded by #S` and closing the original, read the original's `/dependencies/blocking`. For each open dependant:
  - Add a native `blocked_by` edge to `#S`. Keep the old edge as history, or remove it; either is fine.
  - Replace `#<original>` with `#S` on `Blocked by:` lines only, using the signed write wrapper.
  - Post one short pointer comment.
- Also add a reconciler sweep in `dependency-event-reconciler.sh` for edges that already exist. It applies the same rewrite whenever every native blocker is closed and a trusted successor is open.
- Gotcha: `gh issue view --json body,blockedBy` can serve stale data for a short time after writes. Verify with `gh api repos/O/R/issues/N` and `/dependencies/blocked_by`, or GraphQL, before reporting.

## Verification

Add a case to `tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh`: a dependant blocked only by a superseded original gains an edge to the successor and has its body line rewritten, and a dependant with an open blocker is left alone.

title: headless workers: read-wide, write-narrow — read-only sibling worktrees, read-only toolchain roots, canonical-checkout redirect
body:
## What

Give headless workers a read-wide, write-narrow filesystem boundary:

1. **Sibling worktrees become read-only for workers.** A headless worker may read anything under the worktree base, but `edit`, `write` and `apply_patch` (and mutating `git -C <path>` commands) may only target its own `WORKER_WORKTREE_PATH`, plus managed temp under `AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR`.
2. **Read-only toolchain roots are allowed without a maintainer.** Allow `read`/`glob`/`grep`/`list` (never writes) under `~/.nvm/**`, still filtered by the broker's `FORBIDDEN_PATTERN`.
3. **Canonical checkout requests get an owned redirect instead of a maintainer hold:** "read the same tracked path in your own worktree; install dependencies worktree-locally." The canonical checkout stays non-grantable to workers.

Interactive sessions are unchanged. Cross-repository linked-worktree writes stay allowed there, as `tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs` ("allows cross-repository linked writes only inside the trusted Git workspace") asserts.

## Why

- **Workers can currently write to other workers' worktrees.** Both permission generators allow the whole worktree base: `.agents/scripts/lib/agent_config.py` `managed_external_directories()` (around line 63) and `.agents/scripts/generate-runtime-config-agents.sh` (around lines 431–432). An OpenCode `external_directory: allow` covers writes as well as reads, and `quality-hooks-git-safety.mjs` doesn't fence headless writes to `WORKER_WORKTREE_PATH`. A confused worker could therefore edit or commit in a concurrent worker's checkout. Reading other worktrees is useful (salvaging prepared files from stale drafts, comparing approaches). Writing to them is never part of a worker's job.
- **Permission-request evidence.** I scanned 51 issues in one managed repo that carried "Maintainer permission required" comments:
  - 26 were read-only `~/.nvm/*` requests, each pausing a worker for a maintainer.
  - 28 targeted the canonical checkout (22 via bash, 6 via read).
  - 0 targeted sibling worktrees, which confirms reads there already work.

  Temp-path requests are covered separately by #35128.

## How

### Write fence: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-git-safety.mjs`

When `isHeadless()` and `WORKER_WORKTREE_PATH` is set, reject `edit`/`write`/`apply_patch` targets that resolve (physically, symlinks resolved) outside that worktree and outside managed temp. For bash, reject mutating git verbs whose `-C`/`--git-dir`/`cd` target is another worktree:

`add`, `commit`, `checkout`, `switch`, `reset`, `restore`, `stash`, `clean`, `merge`, `rebase`, `push`, `worktree remove`

Return an owned message: "Sibling worktrees are read-only for workers. Copy what you need into your own worktree."

Reuse the existing physical-path helpers (`pathIsWithin` in `pre-edit-check-tool.mjs`).

### Read-only roots: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker.mjs`

In headless mode, auto-reply `once` to `external_directory` requests where:
- the tool is `read`, `glob`, `grep` or `list`;
- every pattern is bounded under a declared read-only root (start with `~/.nvm`);
- no pattern matches `FORBIDDEN_PATTERN`.

Log each auto-reply as a blocker-state event, the same way grants are logged. Keep the root list in one constant so it can be extended deliberately.

### Canonical redirect: `.agents/scripts/worker-permission-helper.sh`

Classify canonical-checkout targets, i.e. the registered canonical path from `repos.json` for any repo. Return the owned-recovery redirect above instead of creating a maintainer request.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-git-safety.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/worker-permission-helper.sh`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-permission-helper.sh`

### Verification

- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs` covers:
  - headless write to a sibling worktree → rejected;
  - headless write to own worktree → allowed;
  - interactive cross-repo linked write → still allowed;
  - headless `git -C <sibling> commit` → rejected.
- A broker test covers:
  - headless `read ~/.nvm/versions/*` → auto `once`;
  - `write ~/.nvm/*` → normal gate;
  - `~/.nvm/.../etc/npmrc` → still non-grantable.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-permission-helper.sh` covers: canonical-checkout request → redirect, no request record.
- ShellCheck is clean on changed shell files.

title: GNU stat stdout pollutes BSD fallback assertions in dirty backup regression tests
body:
Observed after merged PR #35151 at commit 0552db9e27ee5ed64cbe2fbfeafe798d7c95fe64: bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dirty-worktree-backup-helper.sh reports 5 passes and 1 failure on Linux. Fix the existing mode assertions in .agents/scripts/tests/test-dirty-worktree-backup-helper.sh and .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-recovery-helper.sh (the latter contains the same BSD-first stat fallback around its sync round-trip check). Use a platform-appropriate existing stat helper or select the platform before capturing output; do not weaken expected permissions or backup checks. Discover other exact occurrences in these touched test files and keep scope limited. Verification: run the existing dirty backup suite on Linux with GNU stat and macOS with BSD stat, and the relevant canonical sync/restore regressions; require all assertions to pass and ShellCheck the changed shell tests. Reference pattern: mode assertions should compare only a mode value, never stdout from a failing first command. No private project data or canonical cleanup is needed to reproduce.

## Agent doc simplification (automated scan)

**File:** `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`
**Detected topic:** Recoverable Worktree Archives
**Current size:** 500 lines

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`

### Classify before acting

**First, determine the file type** — the correct action depends on whether this is an instruction doc or a reference corpus:

- **Instruction doc** (agent rules, workflows, decision trees, operational procedures): Tighten prose, reorder by importance, split if multiple concerns. Follow guidance below.
- **Reference corpus** (SKILL.md, domain knowledge base, textbook-style content with self-contained sections): Do NOT compress content. Instead, split into chapter files with a slim index. See `tools/code-review/code-simplifier.md` "Reference corpora" classification (GH#6432).

### For instruction docs — proposed action

Tighten and restructure this agent doc. Follow `tools/build-agent/build-agent.md` guidance. Key principles:

1. **Preserve all institutional knowledge** — every verbose rule exists because something broke without it. Do not remove task IDs, incident references, error statistics, or decision rationale. Compress prose, not knowledge.
2. **Order by importance** — most critical instructions first (primacy effect: LLMs weight earlier context more heavily). Security rules, core workflow, then edge cases.
3. **Split if needed** — if the file covers multiple distinct concerns, extract sub-docs with a parent index. Use progressive disclosure (pointers, not inline content).
4. **Use search patterns, not line numbers** — any `file:line_number` references to other files go stale on every edit. Use `rg "pattern"` or section heading references instead.

### For reference corpora — proposed action

1. **Extract each major section** into its own file (e.g., `01-introduction.md`, `02-fundamentals.md`)
2. **Replace the original with a slim index** (~100-200 lines) — table of contents with one-line descriptions and file pointers
3. **Zero content loss** — every line moves to a chapter file, nothing is deleted or compressed
4. **Reconcile existing chapter files** — if partial splits already exist, deduplicate and keep the most complete version

### Worker guidance

**Reference pattern:** `.agents/reference/large-file-split.md` (playbook for splits — covers orchestrator pattern, identity-key preservation, and PR body template).

**Precedent in this repo:** `issue-sync-helper.sh` + `issue-sync-lib.sh` (simple split) and `headless-runtime-lib.sh` + sub-libraries (complex split). For agent docs, see existing chapter-file splits in `.agents/reference/`.

**Expected CI gate overrides:** If this PR triggers a complexity regression from restructured files, apply the `complexity-bump-ok` label AND include a `## Complexity Bump Justification` section in the PR body citing scanner evidence. See the playbook section 4 (Known CI False-Positive Classes).

title: Playwright MCP native tool filenames resolve against the client root and write into canonical checkouts (GH#34111 gap)
body:
## Observed failure (follow-up to GH#34111)

On 2026-10-15 an interactive OpenCode session delegated a read-only dark-mode check to a `playwright` subagent. The prompt said screenshots may only go under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/`. The child called `playwright_browser_take_screenshot` with `filename: "<name>.png"` (a bare relative name), twice. Both images, viewport screenshots of a client's website, were written to the root of the **canonical checkout** of an unrelated plugin repository: the session's project directory. The child then searched the MCP session artifact folder, could not find the files and reported "could not verify either as a file". The parent did not check `git status`.

The files stayed there for 4 days. Every canonical fast-forward in that time (41 merges) made a new dirty-worktree backup holding the same two untracked images: 41 `refs/aidevops/dirty-worktree-backups/*` refs in the project repository plus 41 copies under `tmp/dirty-main-backups/`. Nothing alerted the owner, who found them in a session's closing `git status`. Nothing was pushed: origin had only heads, tags and PR refs.

Earlier dirty backups for other repositories show the same pattern (an untracked `.playwright-mcp/` folder, and many `*-desktop.png`, `*-mobile.png` or `*-dark.png` files in canonical roots), so this was not a one-off.

## Root cause (verified in source)

GH#34111 made the Playwright MCP process start in a private per-session folder (`mcp-registry.mjs` launcher: `cd -- "$output_dir"; exec "$@" --output-dir "$output_dir"`; `browser-mcp-launcher.sh` likewise). That covers raw `page.screenshot({path})` in run-code. It does **not** cover the `filename` argument of the native tools, because `@playwright/mcp@0.0.79` (`playwright-core/lib/coreBundle.js`) resolves those against the **MCP client root**, not the process cwd and not `--output-dir`:

- `initializeServer`: when the client advertises the `roots` capability, `clientInfo.cwd = firstRootPath(await server.listRoots())`; it falls back to `process.cwd()` only when there are no roots (`allRootPaths`, ~l.71524).
- `Response.resolveClientFile` → `resolveClientFilename(filename)` → `workspaceFile(options, fileName, this._clientWorkspace)` → `path.resolve(options.cwd, fileName)` (~l.64699, 65204-65216).
- `checkFile` allows any path inside `outputDir` **or** the client workspace (~l.64720), so the write is allowed.

OpenCode advertises the session's project directory as the root, so `filename: "x.png"` lands in `<project>/x.png`. Screenshots without `filename` go to `--output-dir` as expected. The comment above the `playwright` registry entry ("explicit relative output filenames remaining within that directory") is incorrect for 0.0.79. The same resolution applies to `browser_snapshot`, `browser_pdf_save`, storage-state, video and response-body `filename`s.

## Proposed fix

1. **Runtime confinement (primary).** In the Playwright launch path, put a minimal stdio JSON-RPC filter between client and server that removes `params.capabilities.roots` from the client's `initialize` request, and does not forward `roots/list` or `notifications/roots/list_changed`. Playwright then falls back to `process.cwd()`, which is already the private artifact folder, so every relative `filename` lands under the session's artifact root. No CLI option exists for this (`allowUnrestrictedFileAccess` widens access instead). Keep the pinned version and the `mcp-diagnose.sh` version check working. Correct the registry comment.
2. **Surface stray artifacts instead of re-backing them up silently.** When the canonical fast-forward or recovery path finds untracked files that byte-match an existing open or acknowledged backup, do not make another backup. Raise one actionable owner notice (session greeting or pulse) listing the paths, and offer the existing verified `clean` path. Untracked media (`*.png|jpg|webp|pdf|webm`) or `.playwright-mcp/` at a canonical root should be classed as likely agent artifacts in that notice.
3. **Delegation guard.** After a browser-capable child (`playwright`, `playwriter`, `chrome-devtools`) returns, have the parent or plugin compare `git status --porcelain` of the session directory before and after the call. Report any new untracked paths in the child's result. Update `tools/browser/browser-automation.md` and `workflows/ui-verification.md`: until (1) ships, omit `filename` on native screenshot tools (or give an absolute path inside the reported output dir), and a child that "cannot find" its screenshot must check the project directory.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs`: the Playwright launcher (~l.776-805) and the registry comment (~l.439).
- `.agents/scripts/browser-mcp-launcher.sh`: the same filter for the non-plugin config path.
- `.agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-helper.sh` and/or `.agents/scripts/dirty-worktree-backup-helper.sh`: dedupe identical untracked payloads; owner notice.
- `.agents/tools/browser/browser-automation.md`, `.agents/workflows/ui-verification.md`: guidance.
- Tests next to the existing launcher/registry tests (discover their exact paths; do not guess).

## Verification

- In a disposable Git repository opened as the OpenCode project, call `browser_take_screenshot` with `filename: "probe.png"`, with no filename, and run-code `page.screenshot({path: "./probe2.png"})`. All three files are under the per-session artifact root; `git status --porcelain` of the project is empty; the tool's printable link still reads back.
- `browser_snapshot` with `filename` behaves the same.
- A canonical fast-forward with a stray untracked image creates at most one backup, and a second fast-forward makes no new backup but raises one notice.
- `mcp-diagnose.sh check-all` still reports the pinned Playwright version.

This brief omits project identity, customer content and private paths.

title: OpenCode 2: gpt_image_generate OAuth always fails — v2.mjs does not pass imageOAuthAccountResolver to createTools
body:
## Summary

On OpenCode 2, `gpt_image_generate` with the default `auth: "oauth"` always fails with:

```
OpenAI OAuth account selection is unavailable in this runtime.
```

even when the OpenAI OAuth pool has an active account.

## Cause

`createTools()` (`plugins/opencode-aidevops/tools.mjs`) passes `options.imageOAuthAccountResolver` / `imageOAuthAccountRotator` / `imageFetch` into `createGptImageTool()`. `gpt-image-auth.mjs` `resolveOAuthAuth()` throws when the resolver is not a function.

- `index.mjs` (OpenCode 1) passes `imageFetch`, `imageOAuthAccountResolver: selectOpenAIRequestAccount` and `imageOAuthAccountRotator`.
- `v2.mjs` (OpenCode 2) calls `createTools(SCRIPTS_DIR, run, {...})` without any of the three, so the OAuth path can never work on OpenCode 2.

## Environment

- aidevops 3.39.47
- OpenCode Desktop 2.0.28 (macOS), plugin loaded via `v2.mjs`

## Local workaround (verified offline)

In `v2.mjs`, import `selectOpenAIRequestAccount` from `./oauth-pool.mjs` and add to the `createTools` options:

```js
imageFetch: globalThis.fetch?.bind(globalThis),
imageOAuthAccountResolver: selectOpenAIRequestAccount,
```

With that, `resolveGptImageAuth({ auth: "oauth" }, { resolveOAuthAccount: selectOpenAIRequestAccount })` returns `mode: "oauth"` with the pooled account.

The rotator was deliberately left out: `rotateOpenAIPoolToken()` → `applyOpenAIPoolAccount()` rewrites `process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY` and calls `client.auth.set`, which is the OpenCode 1 provider-auth path and may conflict with `v2-provider-auth.mjs`. An OpenCode 2-safe rotator (select next pool account without mutating provider auth) would be the full fix.

## Suggested fix

Pass an image OAuth resolver (and an OpenCode 2-safe rotator) from `v2.mjs`, and add an OpenCode 2 wiring test alongside `tests/test-gpt-image-tool.mjs`.

title: t18741: headless workers can't finish cross-repo workflow rollouts unattended
body:
## Why

A cross-repo workflow rollout (`sync-workflows-helper.sh --apply`) should run to the end without a person stepping in. That is what makes framework fixes reach every managed repository.

In #35096 it did not. For about 12 hours, 6 headless dispatches across 3 runners each claimed the issue, failed, and released it (`runner_capability_unmet`). Two steps had to be done by hand in an interactive session:

1. **The last caller refresh could not be pushed.** That repository uses an SSH remote. Sandboxed workers never get `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`; this is deliberate (GH#33064, `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-attempt.sh`), so that model processes cannot use the user's SSH agent. As a result, any SSH remote fails in a worker with `Permission denied (publickey)`. The same command worked at once in an interactive session on the same machine.
2. **The worker could not merge the pilot refresh PR.** The headless PR-only scope check looked up the framework issue (#35096) in the downstream repository, got HTTP 404, and blocked the merge.

The second cause also affects every other headless task that opens a PR outside its issue's repository. The first affects every helper that runs Git network commands on an SSH remote from a worker.

## Done when

- A headless worker can fetch from and push to a GitHub repository whose remote uses SSH, by authenticating with the `gh` credential it already has. It must not get SSH agent access.
- A headless worker can merge a PR in repository B for an issue it was dispatched in repository A, and the issue's PR-only contract still blocks the merge where it applies.
- Same-repository behaviour is unchanged.

## Where

- Merge scope: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-authority.sh` `_merge_headless_pr_only_scope_clear`. In progress in PR #35163.
- Git transport: `.agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh` fetch (~L303, ~L1150) and push (~L1263). The existing pattern to reuse is `_worktree_fetch_origin_branch` in `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh` (SSH auth failure → one retry over HTTPS with `gh auth git-credential`).

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh`
- `shellcheck` on changed scripts
- Product path: `sync-workflows-helper.sh --workflow loc-badge --json` dry-run still classifies repositories, and an `--apply` against a repository with an SSH remote works without `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` set.

Ref #35096

title: gh-write-helper review-handoff: idempotent no-op and reason codes instead of opaque 'GitHub write failed'
body:
## Observed

In an interactive `/full-loop` on a managed project repo, `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` created a draft PR and set the linked issue to `status:in-review`. After `gh pr ready`, the documented step 4.3 handoff was run:

```text
gh-write-helper.sh issue review-handoff <issue> --repo <owner/repo> --pr <pr>
[aidevops][gh-write-helper][ERROR] GitHub write failed (exit 1).
```

The issue was already in the target state (`status:in-review`, assigned to the actor, open; PR open, non-draft, authored by the actor, closing reference present). Nothing was wrong, but the output read like a failed GitHub write and needed manual label inspection to rule out a real failure.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh` `_issue_review_handoff` (around lines 40-45) requires `status:in-progress` present and `status:in-review` absent. When the issue is already in review, the `jq -e` precondition returns 1 with no diagnostic, and `main` reports the generic "GitHub write failed" message. The same silent `return 1` applies to each failed check in `_gh_verify_owned_review_handoff_pr` (`.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh` around lines 391-412: actor lookup, issue assignee, PR state/draft/author/closing reference).

`workflows/full-loop.md` / `scripts/commands/full-loop.md` step 4.3 says `commit-and-pr` handles status bookkeeping, then still presents `review-handoff` for "workers and managed manual PRs", so interactive sessions run it after `commit-and-pr` and hit this path.

## Expected

- Already `status:in-review` with valid ownership/linkage: exit 0 with an explicit no-op line (for example `REVIEW_HANDOFF=already-in-review`), with no label mutation and no audit exemption.
- Each failed precondition: a specific stderr reason (`issue-not-in-progress`, `issue-not-assigned-to-actor`, `pr-draft`, `pr-not-authored-by-actor`, `pr-missing-closing-reference`, `api-unavailable`) and a non-zero exit distinct from a real write failure.
- Fail-closed behaviour and audit provenance stay unchanged; only the diagnostics and the idempotent no-op are new.

## How

- `_issue_review_handoff`: idempotent no-op plus reason codes.
- `_gh_verify_owned_review_handoff_pr`: reason codes on stderr.
- `full-loop.md` step 4.3: state that the handoff is unnecessary after `commit-and-pr` already set `status:in-review`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/commands/full-loop.md`

## Verification

- Existing gh-write-helper / safe-edit tests pass; ShellCheck is clean.
- Manual: on an issue already `status:in-review`, `review-handoff` exits 0 with the no-op line and makes no label change; on an issue with a draft PR, it exits non-zero with `pr-draft`.

title: Git-only recovery with shared worktree creation and capture timings
body:
## Objective

Implement the operator-approved Git-only recovery contract: preserve reachable HEAD commits plus separate staged/unstaged binary patches. Treat untracked/ignored files and raw Git administration as outside recovery, without project-specific directory exceptions.

## Implementation scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.sh` and `worktree_archive_snapshot.py`: explicit Git-only capture, exact base/HEAD, incremental bundle, two patches; no verification or trial restore inside capture.
- `worktree_recovery_producer.py`, `worktree_recovery_migrate.py`, `worktree_recovery_migration_state.py`, `worktree_recovery_retire.py`: new receipts say archived, not restore-verified; existing receipts retain their policy; preserve source-removal guards.
- `worktree_archive_restore.py`: import saved commits and reuse `worktree-helper.sh add`, the same creation/registration entrypoint used by `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`; apply staged then unstaged patches.
- `worktree_recovery_timing.py` and the recovery documentation: private per-attempt/stage timings and an explicit distinction between capture, verification and removal.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.md`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_snapshot.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py`

Exercise committed history, simultaneous staged/unstaged changes, binary changes, additions/deletions/rename, and excluded ignored nested repositories. Assert capture does not invoke verify or restore. Run scoped lint and a source-preserving archive capture against a real private application recovery input; retain private paths and evidence locally, not in this issue.

The operator clarified that external regression testing is mandatory: the ban is

the real application repository. Preserve the existing profile full-preservation
checks by explicitly selecting their legacy policy; run the affected suites.

title: fix(pulse): blocked-checkpoint attention comment reposts every cycle because empty attempt field collapses TSV parse
body:
## What

`_pcc_blocked_attention` in `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` reposts the same `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` comment on every pulse cycle, instead of once per PR head and blocked release. Each repost carries `attempt=true`, which shows the cause.

## Evidence

- Three managed repos each got the same comment for the same `pr=`/`head=`/`release=` key 3-4 times within ~3 hours on 2026-10-20 (roughly 02:58, 04:25, 05:00, 05:41 and 06:29 UTC). Every repost shows `attempt=true`.
- `_pcc_blocked_release_evidence` (around line 584) prints `release_id<TAB>attempt<TAB>posted` with `@tsv`. When no `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=ready` attempt exists, `$attempt` is `""`. The output is then `ID\t\ttrue`.
- `_pcc_blocked_attention` (around line 692) parses this with `IFS=$'\t' read -r release_id attempt posted`. Tab is IFS whitespace, so bash merges the two tabs into one. `attempt` becomes `true` and `posted` comes out empty. The `posted == "true"` dedup check therefore always fails and the helper posts again.

## Fix

- Make the empty attempt field survive parsing. Either emit a non-whitespace placeholder (for example `-`) for an empty attempt and map it back to empty, or use a non-whitespace delimiter such as `\^_` in the jq output and `IFS=$'\x1f'` in the read.
- Check `_pcc_completed_release_evidence` and other `@tsv` + `IFS=$'\t' read` pairs in the same file for the same empty-middle-field bug.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`

## Reference pattern

The existing test around line 513 of `tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` checks that one comment is posted. Add a case with no `phase=ready` lease and assert that a second call prints `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION_EXISTS` and does not post again.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`

title: Bounded operation must reject dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh dispatch (drains detached worker)
body:
## What

`aidevops_bounded_operation` rejects only `pulse-wrapper.sh --command dispatch|dispatch-foss` as a detaching launcher. It still accepts `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh dispatch NUMBER SLUG`, and its exit-time drain then kills the detached worker. The `automate` agent's Quick Reference names that helper as the issue-dispatch path, so a supervisor that wraps a slow dispatch (more than 120 s) in a bounded operation kills its own worker and strands a live-looking claim.

## Observed evidence (2026-10-20, supervisor pulse)

- Bounded operation `["bash", ".../dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh", "dispatch", "<N>", "<owner/repo>"]` exited 0 after about 160 s with `post_exit_descendants_terminated=true`.
- The worker log shows lifecycle up to `worker_start` and `db_isolated`, then `Terminated`. The worker ran inside a `systemd_scope` and the scope was gone afterwards.
- Side effects left behind: issue at `status:queued` and self-assigned, a `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=ready` with about 2 h left, and a ledger entry for the dead PID. An immediate redispatch was refused (`Active worker already owns this issue (ledger)`, then `ASSIGNED ... to <self>`) until `dispatch-ledger-helper.sh expire` ran and the stale-assignment window passed.

## How

1. In `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-values.mjs`, extend `detachingLauncherError` so it also rejects `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` whose first argument is `dispatch`, through the same `launchedArgv` normalisation (env prefix, `bash script.sh`). Reuse the existing message shape and point to the normal shell tool.
2. Add the matching case to `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-operation-dispatch-launcher.mjs`, following its existing pulse-wrapper cases.
3. Optional: in `.agents/automate.md` Dispatch Protocol, add one line saying dispatch must run through the normal shell tool, never a bounded operation.

## Verification

- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-operation-dispatch-launcher.mjs`
- The bounded operation now refuses `["bash", "<agents>/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh", "dispatch", "1", "o/r"]` before spawn, so no claim is created. `status` and other subcommands are still allowed.

- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-operation-dispatch-launcher.mjs`

title: fix(opencode): replay verbatim user input and images after compaction so authorisations and attachments survive
body:
## Problem

In long-running OpenCode sessions, two things do not survive context compaction:

1. **User-attached images.** After compaction the model can no longer see screenshots or images the user attached earlier.
2. **User instructions, especially authorisations** (merge, release, standing corrections). After compaction the agent asks again or acts as if they were never given.

## Root causes (OpenCode 1.19.3 source, `packages/opencode/src/session/`)

1. **The summarizer never sees images.** `compaction.ts` `serialize()` turns every user file part into the text `[Attached image/png: <filename>]` before the summary request. Pasted images usually have no useful filename and no local path, so the summary can at best say an image existed.
2. **Pre-compaction messages leave model context.** `message-v2.ts` `filterCompacted()` sends only `[compaction user, summary, retained tail…]`. The original user messages, including their image parts, are no longer sent, even though they are still stored in the session database.
3. **The retained tail usually drops the latest user message.** `compaction.ts` `select()`/`splitTurn()` keeps 2K–15K tokens of recent context. When the current turn is larger than that, which is normal for long tool-heavy turns, the split starts at `turn.start + 1`. The turn's own user message, with its authorisation and screenshots, is moved into the summarized head.
4. **Authorisations exist only as an LLM paraphrase, in assistant voice.** The summary is an assistant message regenerated on every compaction from the previous summary. Each pass loses more detail, and the result is not attributed to the user.
5. **aidevops rules then discount that paraphrase.** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction.mjs` asks the summarizer to quote authorisations verbatim. It also says "a summary never widens scope, permissions, or authority" and "Historical commands are evidence, not authorization". `reference/session.md:361` repeats that compaction cannot widen authority. A resumed agent correctly treats a summarized authorisation as unproven and asks again. The framework gives it no trusted, user-attributed record to rely on instead.

The prompt-only fix (asking the summarizer to quote) cannot fix this, because the paraphrase is the wrong carrier.

## Fix

Deterministic replay of verbatim user input after compaction, from the session record:

- New plugin module `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-pinned-input.mjs`, wired into `messagesTransformHook` in `index.mjs`. When the request starts with a completed compaction summary, it fetches the session's stored messages once per compaction (`client.session.messages`). It collects the user-authored (non-synthetic, non-ignored) text and media parts that are no longer visible, and prepends them to the compaction user message. That message is the one the summary answers.
- Budgets keep it bounded: about 32K characters of text (first and most recent messages kept, middle elided with a marker) and the 4 most recent images (`data:` URLs only). Earlier media becomes labelled placeholders. Images are not replayed after an overflow compaction. Fails open, can be turned off with env vars, and is cached per compaction so the prompt-cache prefix stays stable.
- The replay header states the text is the user's own words, replayed by the plugin, carrying the same authority as when first sent, with later input taking precedence.
- Summary rules and `reference/session.md` now say that authorisations come from verbatim user input, replayed or live, not from the summary's paraphrase. The summary still never widens authority.

## Files

- NEW `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-pinned-input.mjs`
- EDIT `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs` (`messagesTransformHook`)
- EDIT `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction.mjs` (`compactionSummaryRules`)
- EDIT `.agents/reference/session.md` "Context Compaction Resilience"

## Verification

- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-compaction-checkpoint-scope.mjs` plus the full plugin test suite
- Run the new transform directly on a synthetic compacted message list (text, image, synthetic, overflow cases)
- Manual: in a session, paste a screenshot and give an authorisation, run `/compact`, then ask what the screenshot showed and whether merge was authorised

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

- `quality-hooks-image.mjs` `applyImageSizeGuard` expects provider-shape `content[]` but the V1 `messages.transform` hook receives `{info, parts}`, so the guard never runs on OpenCode 1.x.
- Parity for OpenCode 2 (`v2.mjs`) and Claude Code (no PreCompact/SessionStart compact hook re-injects user input).

title: fix(opencode): image size guard never runs on OpenCode 1.x messages.transform shape
body:
## Problem

`applyImageSizeGuard()` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-image.mjs` (GH#21793) never acts on OpenCode 1.x.

## Evidence

- `index.mjs` `messagesTransformHook` calls `applyImageSizeGuard(output, qualityLog)` from `experimental.chat.messages.transform`.
- OpenCode v1.19.3 `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts:1255` triggers that hook with `{ messages: msgs }`, where `msgs` are stored `WithParts` objects shaped like `{ info: { role }, parts: [{ type: "file", mime, url }] }`.
- `guardUserMessage()` returns at once unless `message.role === "user"` and `Array.isArray(message.content)`, and `checkImagePart()` matches only `{ type: "image", source: { type: "base64" } }`. That is the Anthropic provider shape, which never reaches this hook in V1.

Oversized user images therefore reach the provider unguarded. This matters more now that GH#35186 replays recent images after compaction.

## Fix

Teach the guard the V1 shape. For `info.role === "user"` messages, inspect `parts` with `type === "file"`, an `image/*` mime and a `data:` URL. Compute the decoded size from the base64 payload, then downscale (reuse `tryDownscale`) or replace the part with the existing rejection text part. Keep the current provider-shape path for any caller that still uses it.

## Files

- EDIT `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-image.mjs` (`guardUserMessage`, `checkImagePart`)
- Reference pattern: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-pinned-input.mjs` for V1 `{info, parts}` handling

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-image.mjs`

## Reproducer

Pass the V1-shaped message from Verification to `applyImageSizeGuard`. On `main` the 6 MB part comes back unchanged and nothing is logged, because `guardUserMessage` returns at its `message.role`/`message.content` check.

## Verification

- `npm test --prefix .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops`
- Run `applyImageSizeGuard({ messages: [{ info: { role: "user" }, parts: [{ type: "file", mime: "image/png", url: "data:image/png;base64,<6MB>" }] }] })` and confirm the part is downscaled or replaced.

title: feat: compaction user-input replay parity for OpenCode 2 and Claude Code
body:
## Problem

GH#35186 / PR #35187 replays verbatim user input and recent images after compaction on OpenCode 1.x only. OpenCode 2 and Claude Code sessions still lose attached images and keep user authorisations only as the summary's paraphrase.

## Context

- OpenCode 1 implementation: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-pinned-input.mjs`, wired in `index.mjs` `messagesTransformHook`.
- OpenCode 2 adapter: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs` (compaction hook at about line 474). Its message and transform contract differs and must be checked against the installed 2.x host before choosing the injection point.
- Claude Code: no PreCompact or SessionStart (`source: "compact"`) hook in `.agents/hooks/`. A SessionStart compact hook can add text context, such as verbatim user prompts read from the session transcript under `~/.claude/projects/`. Re-injecting images may not be possible there; if so, list attachment paths instead.

## Fix

1. OpenCode 2: find the transform hook that sees post-compaction model messages, then reuse `collectHiddenUserInput` / `selectWithinBudget` / `buildReplayParts` through a shape adapter.
2. Claude Code: add a SessionStart hook for `compact` that replays the user's verbatim prompts from the transcript under the same budget and provenance header. Register it in the Claude Code setup path next to the existing hooks.

Exact paths for the Claude Code hook registration are unknown until the setup code is inspected (`rg -n "SessionStart|session_continuation_stop" .agents/scripts .agents/hooks`).

title: Pulse: single-owner run:custom/scripts routines record failures on every non-owner host
body:
## What

Pulse routines that run a host-private adapter (`run:custom/scripts/<name>.sh`) need a way to be scoped to their owner host. Non-owner hosts should skip such a routine silently instead of recording a failure.

## Why (observed evidence)

Project repos use single-owner routines: one maintainer host installs the adapter, and the routine entry in `TODO.md` is enabled for every Pulse host that registers the repo. On every other host, `_routine_execute` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh:684-697` logs `script not found or not executable` and calls `_routine_finalize_terminal ... FAILURE` on every due slot.

Observed on a non-owner host on 2026-10-20: a twice-daily single-owner report routine had `last_status: failure, consecutive_failures: 15` in `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/routine-state.json`. Meanwhile its real owner (another maintainer's host) published successfully about twice a day. A second single-owner routine added the same day (every 2 hours) will add about 12 failures per day on each non-owner host. These failures are noise. They hide real routine failures, and they push maintainers towards installing a second adapter, which the project runbooks forbid because it creates competing writers.

## How (proposal; worker decides between options)

- **Option A (smallest):** in `_routine_execute`, when `run_script` resolves under `custom/scripts/` and the file is absent, log `routine <id>: owner adapter not installed on this host; skipping` and record a distinct non-failure status (for example `skipped_not_owner`) that does not increment `consecutive_failures`. A present but non-executable file stays a failure.
- **Option B:** an optional `host:<hostname>` (or `owner:<instance>`) field parsed in `_routine_parse_line` (`pulse-routines.sh:981-1019`), next to `run:`/`agent:`. Non-matching hosts skip the routine before `is-due`.

Files: `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh` (`_routine_execute`, `_routine_parse_line`, `_routine_finalize_terminal`), `.agents/reference/routines.md` (document the behaviour), and the existing pulse-routines tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/` if present.

## Acceptance

- [ ] On a host without the adapter, a due `run:custom/scripts/<missing>.sh` routine does not increase `consecutive_failures` and logs one clear skip line.
- [ ] A present but failing adapter still records `failure` exactly as today.
- [ ] `reference/routines.md` documents how single-owner routines behave on non-owner hosts.
### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh`
- `.agents/reference/routines.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-routines-owner-adapter.sh`

title: GH#35189 follow-up: harden compaction replay boundaries, rendered budget and V2 store growth
body:
## Description

Follow-up from the independent review of PR #35196 (GH#35189, compaction user-input replay for OpenCode 2 and Claude Code). The review's major findings were fixed in that PR. These residual hardening items were deferred because they affect the replay format shared by OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2 and Claude Code, or are bounded in practice.

1. **Forgeable replay boundaries.** Replayed user text is inserted as-is between `### User message i of N` headings and the `--- End of replayed user input. ---` marker. A user turn containing those literal strings (for example, a pasted transcript) can make later text look like it sits outside the replay. Fix: add a per-render nonce to the headings and end marker, and state the nonce in the header. Apply the same change to every renderer so the format stays consistent.
2. **Rendered size isn't bounded by the budget.** `select_within_budget()` / `selectWithinBudget()` count only message text. Headings, timestamps, attachment notes and excerpt markers are not counted. Attachment-only turns cost zero. With `AIDEVOPS_COMPACTION_REPLAY_MAX_CHARS=0`, every turn still emits a heading. Fix: count the rendered length (or a fixed per-turn overhead). Zero should mean disabled, or emit no turns.
3. **OpenCode 2 store rewrites the whole session on each prompt.** `compaction-replay-v2-store.mjs` serializes the full per-session store on every `recordPrompt`. Prompt text has no per-session cap; only the attachment count is pruned. Fix: cap stored text per session (keeping the first turn plus the newest turns), or switch to append-only writes.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-replay-budget.mjs`: shared `buildReplayParts` / `selectWithinBudget` (OpenCode 1 and 2), items 1–2
- `.agents/hooks/compaction_user_input_replay.py`: `render()` and `select_within_budget()` (Claude Code), items 1–2
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-replay-v2-store.mjs`: `writeStore` and the prompt cap, item 3

### Files Scope

Dependency: PR #35196 (GH#35189) is merged, so all three target files now exist on `main`; rebase/start from current `main`.

- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-replay-budget.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/hooks/compaction_user_input_replay.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/hooks/compaction_replay_transcript.py` (only if the Claude Code renderer/budget lives here)
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-replay-v2-store.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-replay-v2.mjs` (only if the V2 render call site must pass the nonce)
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs`

## Reference pattern

The pruning in `pruneMedia()` and `pruneStores()` in `compaction-replay-v2-store.mjs` shows how the store already bounds attachments and old sessions.

## Verification

- A synthetic transcript whose user turn contains the literal end marker still renders exactly one trusted end marker, carrying the nonce.
- With `AIDEVOPS_COMPACTION_REPLAY_MAX_CHARS=1000` and 500 image-only turns, the rendered context stays within a documented bound.
- `node --test` for `tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs` and the compaction tests passes. `python3 -m py_compile` passes on the hook files. `qlty smells` reports nothing on the touched files.

## Summary

`runtime-events-retention.mjs` silently does nothing (no output, exit 0) when
run through the deployed `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` path, because that path
is a symlink into `runtime-bundles/<id>/agents/` and the entrypoint guard does
not resolve symlinks:

```js
if (process.argv[1] && pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href === import.meta.url) {
```

Node resolves `import.meta.url` to the real bundle path; `argv[1]` keeps the
symlink path, so the guard is false.

## Impact

- Routine `r918` (`observability-helper.sh retention-maintenance --apply`,
  daily 03:10) has never archived anything: inventory shows
  `archive_bytes: 0` and ~538 MB of candidates outside the 30-day window.
  `llm-requests.db` keeps growing (5.2 GiB on the reporting host).
- `observability-helper.sh storage`, `retention --dry-run`, and
  `retention-maintenance --dry-run` all print nothing.
- `storage-inventory-helper.sh status` reports observability as
  "classification unavailable (retention-inventory-unavailable)".

## Reproduce

1. `observability-helper.sh storage --json` -> no output, exit 0.
2. Same command against the resolved bundle path
   (`node "$(readlink -f ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/runtime-events-retention.mjs)" inventory --db <db>`)
   -> prints JSON inventory.

## Same guard pattern elsewhere (check each)

`runtime-events.mjs`, `frontier-harness-report.mjs`,
`task-projection-reducer.mjs`, `team-interface-core.mjs`,
`model-replay-benchmark.mjs`, `playwright-runtime.mjs`,
`playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs`, `higgsfield-mcp-proxy.mjs`,
`routing-feedback.mjs`.

## Suggested fix

- Use one symlink-safe entrypoint helper (reference pattern:
  `isWorkerBlockerEntrypoint` in `worker-blocker-log.mjs`, or
  `realpathSync` on both sides as in `task-coordinator.mjs`).
- Have `observability-helper.sh` fail loudly if the retention CLI exits 0 with

title: worktree-recovery maintenance: small removals reset escalation, so retention advisory never fires while store stays far over cap
body:
## Summary

Worktree recovery maintenance runs and reclaims small amounts, but the
`worktree-recovery-retention` advisory never appears while the legacy store
stays ~20x over the 5 GiB cap. Two mechanisms defeat escalation:

1. **Any removal resets the window.** `_worktree_recovery_maintenance_update_cycle_state`
   deletes `zero-candidate-cycle.json` whenever `SELECTED > 0` or
   `CACHE_SELECTED > 0`, and a completed transaction calls
   `_worktree_recovery_maintenance_update_advisory '{"escalation":{"required":false}}'`
   (clears the advisory). Escalation needs `sustained_scanned >= inventory_count`
   with zero removals in between.
2. **Coverage per run is too low to ever reach that bound.** Runs scan ~40 of
   ~725 buckets (deadline exhausted, ~5% coverage), so ~18 consecutive
   zero-removal runs are needed. In practice a sub-megabyte removal
   (e.g. 143 KB-880 KB) happens every few runs and resets the counter.

Result: the store stays at ~97 GiB with ~94 GiB "protected", and the operator
gets no signal. The contract in `reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`
says maintenance should write the advisory when it cannot get under the cap.

## Evidence (one Linux host, aidevops v3.39.49/50)

- `worktree-helper.sh recovery`: 725 buckets, 706 protected (94.0 GiB),
  19 unknown (3.1 GiB), 0 candidates.
- `recovery legacy-report`: unknown-origin 568, eligible-legacy-pulse 94,
  non-pulse-profile 31, unsafe-metadata 17, source-removal-incomplete 14.
- `cleanup_worktrees.log` outcomes: early runs were
  `operator-intervention-required`; since then a repeating mix of
  `removed` (recent `reclaimed_bytes` mostly 0.1-2 MB), `no-candidates`, and
  `failed`. Never a sustained no-candidate streak long enough to escalate.
- Current `zero-candidate-cycle.json`: inventory 725, scanned_in_cycle 40,
  completed_cycles 0, sustained_scanned 40, pressure_active true.
- Advisory file absent.
- Separate defect in the same log: ~120 runs end with
  `{"outcome":"failed","stage":"selection","reason":"preparation-failed"}`
  with no further detail; these also do not advance the cycle.

## Expected

While pressure is active (store > cap), escalation should be driven by the
store staying over the cap, not by "zero removals in a full sweep". A removal
that reclaims a negligible fraction of the overage should not clear the
advisory or reset the window.

## Suggested fix

- File: `.agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-maintenance-helper.sh`
  - Keep `sustained_scanned` across removals while `pressure_active` stays true;
    reset only when pressure ends or reclaimed bytes bring the store under the cap.
  - In the completed-transaction path, only clear the advisory when
    pressure is no longer active.
  - Optionally add a time-based trigger (e.g. pressure active for > N days).
  - Give `preparation-failed` a sub-reason (which step failed) in the run record.
- Reference pattern: existing `sustained_pressure` / `escalation` jq block in
  `_worktree_recovery_maintenance_no_candidates_json`.

## Verification

- Existing maintenance tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/` for recovery
  maintenance; add a case: pressure active, small removal each run, inventory
  never covered -> advisory written after the threshold.
- On an affected host: advisory appears and names the dominant blocker
  (`archive_worktree_dirty` / unknown origin).

title: worktree-recovery: recognise .venv/dist/tool caches and framework-owned state as regenerable (≈80% of legacy store bytes)
body:
## Summary

On one Linux host the legacy worktree recovery store is ~97 GiB across 725
buckets, and ~80% of those bytes are regenerable build/tool output that the
recovery policy does not recognise. Those dirs make archives `archive-worktree-dirty`
(467 of 725 buckets), so neither bucket apply nor the "protected mixed archive"
cache-root pruning path can reclaim them.

## Evidence (read-only survey of the store)

Bytes by directory name inside recovery buckets (MiB, `du -sm`):

| Dir | MiB | On approved regenerable list? |
|---|---|---|
| `.venv` | 53,438 | no |
| `node_modules` | 14,802 | yes |
| `dist` | 6,930 | no |
| `.mypy_cache` | 1,232 | no |
| `.ruff_cache` | 228 | no |
| `.astro` | 143 | no |
| `build` | 130 | no |
| `*.egg-info` | 75 | no |

Store total: ~99,560 MiB.

The non-cache "dirt" making archives dirty (`git status --porcelain --ignored`,
after removing the approved roots) is dominated by:

- `.ruff_cache/`, `.mypy_cache/`, `.venv/`, `.astro/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `*.egg-info/`
- aidevops' own state: `.agents/loop-state/`, `.agents/tmp/`,
  `.agents/.full-loop-cleanup-deferred`, `todo/batches/*.json.lock`
- OpenCode-generated `.opencode/package.json`, `.opencode/package-lock.json`, `.opencode/.gitignore`

Classifying the 467 dirty buckets by that list: 359 contain only regenerable or
framework-owned ignored content; 108 contain other untracked or modified files.

Example: a 967 MiB bucket whose only ignored content is `.venv` (838 MiB),
`.mypy_cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `__pycache__`, `*.egg-info`, `node_modules`, and
`.agents/loop-state/` (12 KiB). Its tracked tree is clean.

## Expected

- Framework-owned ignored state (`.agents/loop-state/`, `.agents/tmp/`, cleanup
  markers, batch locks) must not make an archive dirty.
- Common regenerable roots (`.venv` and `venv` when they contain `pyvenv.cfg`,
  `.mypy_cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `*.egg-info`, `.astro`, and `dist`/`build` when
  ignored and untracked) should join the approved cache-root list. Use the same
  exact-ignored, untracked, no-symlink, no-tracked-path checks.
- The cache-root pruning path for protected mixed archives should also apply when
  the only blocker is `exact-commit-not-merged`. The cache roots are regenerable
  regardless of commit state, and the archive itself stays.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-*` classifier (approved cache-root identities list)
- `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md` ("Protected mixed archives",
  approved roots list)
- Reference pattern: existing approved list (`node_modules`, `__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, ...)

## Verification

- Recovery plan on an affected host: `archive-worktree-dirty` count drops sharply.
- Maintenance `cache-pruned` outcomes reclaim `.venv`/`dist` roots; store size falls
  substantially while archive code, commits, and patches remain restorable.
- Existing recovery tests extended for one new root type plus a framework-state path.

## Merge Conflict Feedback (from PR #35227)

The previous worker's PR #35227 (`GH#35212: fix(deps): update and trust Source Sans 3`) developed merge conflicts with
`main` that could not be resolved by `gh pr update-branch` (server-side fast-forward).
The conflicts are semantic — the same files were modified on both branches (3 files touched).

### Files in the conflicting PR

```
.agents/configs/trusted-dependabot-updates.conf
bun.lock
packages/gui-web/package.json
```

### Worker guidance

The prior PR's head commit is `e58390b159f09eeb5af1752894e443135c287bf7`. Choose the cheapest path that works:

1. **Cherry-pick onto a fresh branch off current `origin/main`** (~10x cheaper than rewriting, works when the prior implementation was correct-but-stale):

   ```bash
   git fetch origin pull/35227/head:recovered-35227
   # Explicit base on origin/main — NOT canonical HEAD (t2802).
   git worktree add -b fresh-branch ../fresh-worktree origin/main
   cd ../fresh-worktree
   git cherry-pick e58390b159f09eeb5af1752894e443135c287bf7
   # run tests — if clean, proceed to PR
   ```

2. **If cherry-pick surfaces conflicts**, resolve them. The conflict surface IS the semantic overlap between the two branches — resolve those specific hunks rather than rewriting untouched logic.

3. **If the scope-leak warning above fired** (prior PR >20 files but the issue describes a focused fix), **skip cherry-pick entirely** and rebuild from scratch using the issue body as the spec. Do NOT try to cherry-pick-then-drop-files — too error-prone. A clean rewrite from the 2-line spec is cheaper than surgery on a 100-file branch.

4. **Only rewrite from scratch (scope-OK case)** if the prior approach was rejected in review. Check PR #35227's review comments for `CHANGES_REQUESTED` or rejection keywords before assuming the approach was wrong.

Do NOT reuse the old PR's branch directly — always cherry-pick onto a fresh branch off current `origin/main`.

_Routed by deterministic merge pass (pulse-merge.sh)._

title: Runner releases an active worker's claim before its ready lease expires, without CLAIM_RELEASED
body:
## Observed

A Pulse runner released an active worker's claim early, without a `CLAIM_RELEASED` comment, while the worker kept running and finished. The worker then did not open its data PR, and the issue was left `status:available` for a second dispatch.

Timeline on one managed private project repository issue (`<private-repo>#<batch-issue>`, a headless batch issue; aidevops v3.39.50, OpenCode 1.19.0):

- 17:03:10Z `DISPATCH_CLAIM ... max_age_s=1800 phase=prelaunch`
- 17:04:00Z `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=ready ... expires_at=<epoch for 19:04:00Z>`
- 17:25:39Z runner account removed the assignee; 17:25:43Z removed `status:queued`; 17:25:44Z added `status:available`. No comment recorded the release or its reason.
- 17:36:33Z the same worker posted its completion summary (all 10 outcomes published to the project's beta ledger), then ended (32m, 267K tokens).
- No PR referencing the issue was created afterwards. The procedure requires one data PR with `Resolves #<issue>`.

The release came 1h38m before the `ready` lease expiry and before the 1800s claim age (17:33:10Z), so neither expiry explains it.

## Expected

- A runner never releases a claim whose `ready` lease is valid while its worker process is alive, or it terminates the worker first.
- Every release posts `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=<...>` (as the `runner_capability_unmet` path does), so the cause is auditable.
- A worker whose claim was released mid-run either finishes its completion step (PR) or records why it could not.

## Impact

The issue was immediately eligible for redispatch (`status:available` plus `priority:high`). A second worker would have started a new batch under an issue whose work was already done. Committed specs and work logs from the first worker were lost (left on the worker host). The maintainer closed the issue by hand.

## Files to inspect (paths in the framework repo; exact cause unknown)

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` and the stale-claim / recovery paths it calls
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh` / dispatch claim and lease helpers that write `DISPATCH_CLAIM` / `DISPATCH_LEASE`
- `reference/worker-diagnostics.md` for the expected release reasons

## Verification

Reproduce with a worker whose session exceeds ~20 minutes under a `ready` lease: the claim must stay assigned until the worker exits or the lease expires, and any release must post `CLAIM_RELEASED` with a reason.

title: repo-layout migration receipts keep full OpenCode DB backups forever (490 GB observed)
body:
## Problem

`repo_layout_migrate.py apply` copies every OpenCode DB consumer into `<receipt>/backups/opencode-N.db` and never prunes them. Each applied receipt holds a full copy of every session DB.

Observed on one machine (2026-10-20): 4 receipts under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/repo-layout-migrations/` totalling **490 GB** (112–133 GB each). All four journals record `migration:complete`. The newest is from 2026-10-11; the oldest three are superseded by later applied receipts.

These backups lose rollback value quickly. `rollback_database` restores the backup copy, which would discard every session written since the migration. After a later receipt is applied, rolling back an older one is not a coherent operation.

## Proposed fix

- Add a `prune` subcommand (dry-run by default) to `.agents/scripts/repo_layout_migrate.py`. For each receipt in state `applied` (see `receipt_status`, ~line 1989), it removes the large `backups/opencode-*.db` files when either:
  - the receipt is older than a retention window (default 7 days, env-overridable), or
  - a newer applied receipt exists.
- Keep `plan.json`, `receipt.jsonl` and the small backups (`repos.json`, `tabby.yaml`, `recovery-*.json`) so the audit trail survives.
- After pruning, mark database rollback as unavailable in the receipt (append an event), so `rollback` fails closed with a clear message instead of a missing-file error.
- Call `prune --apply` from an existing scheduled path. The weekly `opencode-db-maintenance` routine (`.agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh`) or the pulse preflight next to `system-cleanup.sh` are the natural hosts.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/repo_layout_migrate.py`: backup creation (~1492, `apply_database_consumers` ~1622), `receipt_status` (~1989), `rollback_command` (~2049), `build_parser` (~2120)
- Scheduler host: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh` or `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/repo_layout_migrate.py`
- `.agents/scripts/repo-layout-migrate-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh`
- `tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py`

## Verification

- `prune` dry-run lists only `backups/opencode-*.db` from applied receipts that are past retention or superseded.
- With `--apply`, `du` of the state dir drops accordingly, and `status` still validates the receipt bundle.
- `rollback` on a pruned receipt exits non-zero with an explicit "database backups pruned" reason.

title: OpenCode DB archive/maintenance routines skip per-project isolated session DBs (79 GB event table observed)
body:
## Problem

Interactive OpenCode sessions launched via the aidevops launcher use per-project isolated data dirs at `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/opencode-interactive/project-*/opencode/opencode.db`. The weekly `opencode-db-maintenance` and daily `opencode-db-archive` routines only target the default DB. `OPENCODE_DB` resolves to `${OPENCODE_DATA_DIR}/opencode.db` (`opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh:96`), and the archive log shows only `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` being processed.

Observed on one machine (2026-10-20):

- `opencode-interactive/` totals **128 GB**.
- One project DB is **78.9 GB**. Of that, the `event` table is 69 GB, with 0 free pages, so VACUUM alone reclaims nothing. A second project DB is 32 GB.
- Running `opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh report` inside an interactive session resolves the isolated DB through the session's data dir and shows last maintenance on 2026-07-26. The scheduled archive log (`~/.aidevops/logs/opencode-db-archive.log`) shows only the default DB being processed.

Related: the archive routine *moves* sessions into `opencode-archive.db` (now 29.5 GB) and never expires them, so total OpenCode DB footprint only grows.

## Proposed fix

- Make the archive and maintenance routines enumerate isolated DBs under `opencode-interactive/*/opencode/opencode.db` (bounded, skip DBs held by a live process). Run the existing archive with the same retention and keep-sessions policy on each, with a per-DB archive DB alongside it.
- Add an optional archive-DB retention, e.g. drop `event` rows for archived sessions older than N days while keeping `session`/`message`/`part`, or similar. Default it conservatively and document it.
- Surface per-DB sizes in `opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh report` so the growth is visible.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh` (DB resolution ~96, archive invocation ~1129, report)
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh` (`ACTIVE_DB`/`ARCHIVE_DB`, event copy/delete ~1050)
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-async-helper.sh`
- Isolated data-dir layout: `rg -n "opencode-interactive" .agents/scripts/`

## Verification

- `opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh report` lists every isolated DB with its size.
- A dry run of the archive against an isolated DB reports eligible sessions. After `--apply`, the event table shrinks and the archive DB receives the rows, and a live session's DB is skipped.

title: opencode-tui-capture.py leaves a full DB copy behind when killed (74 GB observed)
body:
## Problem

`opencode-tui-capture.py` copies the full OpenCode DB into a `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="tui-capture-")` under the aidevops tmp root (~line 193–201). If the process is killed (SIGKILL, timeout, terminal close), the context manager never runs and the full copy is left behind.

Observed on one machine (2026-10-20): `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/tui-capture-q6dd0sod/opencode/opencode.db` is **74 GB**, from 2026-10-15, with no open handles (`lsof +D` empty). `system-cleanup.sh` will reap it only after its 7-day retention, so a single interrupted capture can hold tens of GB for a week, and repeated interruptions stack up.

## Proposed fix

- At capture start, reap stale `tui-capture-*` dirs in the temp root that have no live owner. Write an owner PID file into the temp dir and check it on the next run.
- Prefer a cheap copy. Use an APFS clone (`cp -c` / `clonefile`) on macOS when source and target share a volume, or copy only the rows the capture needs (e.g. `sqlite3 .backup` of a filtered DB), instead of `shutil.copyfile` of the whole DB.
- Register signal handlers (SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP) that remove the temp dir before exit.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/opencode-tui-capture.py` (~193–216)
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-test-helper.sh` (caller)
- Reaper precedent: `.agents/scripts/system-cleanup.sh`

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/opencode-tui-capture.py`

## Verification

- Start a capture, kill it with SIGKILL, start another, and confirm the stale `tui-capture-*` dir is removed and the new one works.
- On macOS, the copy step completes in seconds for a multi-GB DB, and `du` shows no extra allocated blocks for the clone.

title: worktree-helper remove: dirty worktree without --force fails after archiving, then retries hit permanent producer:source-drift
body:
## Problem

`worktree-helper.sh remove <path>` without `--force` on a worktree with uncommitted changes fails *after* the recovery archive and producer reservation are created. Output: `Cleanup stopped: the source remains protected and its recoverable archive was retained.` The audit log shows `git-worktree-remove-failed`. Nothing tells the operator the cause is the dirty tree or that `--force` is the supported path.

If the operator then cleans the worktree (e.g. `git checkout -- <file>`) and retries, the retry is refused permanently: `producer:source-drift; existing archive retained` → `guard-refused`. This comes from `reserve()` in `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_producer.py` (~line 132), which compares the current source state with the pinned reservation journal. No documented recovery exists.

Observed 2026-10-20: 8 worktrees whose only change was a lockfile hit exactly this sequence.

Working recovery (verified on all 8): re-apply the archive's own `diff.patch` (`git -C <wt> apply <archive>/diff.patch`) so the source matches the reservation again, then run `worktree-helper.sh remove <wt> --force`. Removal then succeeded and reused the existing archive.

## Proposed fix

1. In `cmd_remove` / `_remove_validate_path` (`.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-cmds.sh`, ~309–376), check for uncommitted changes *before* creating the archive or reservation when `--force` is absent, and fail with an explicit reason: "worktree has uncommitted changes; re-run with --force to archive and remove". `worktree_has_changes` already exists (used at ~229).
2. When the producer returns `source-drift`, print the recovery: restore the recorded state from `<archive>/diff.patch` (plus untracked files) or review and retire the reservation. Add the same text to `.agents/reference/dirty-worktree-preservation.md`.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-cmds.sh` (`_remove_validate_path`, `_remove_cleanup_and_execute` ~427–524)
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_producer.py` (`reserve` ~124)
- `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh` (`remove_archived_worktree_path` ~1754)
- `.agents/reference/dirty-worktree-preservation.md`

## Verification

- Dirty worktree plus `remove` without `--force`: it fails before any new producer archive or transaction appears, and the message names `--force`.
- Dirty worktree, failed attempt, clean, retry: the message explains the drift and the recovery steps.
- Existing tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py` and `.agents/scripts/tests/worktree_recovery_producer_cases.py` pass.

title: full-loop runtime evidence gate rejects descriptive text containing 'no evidence'
body:
## What

`_runtime_evidence_is_substantive` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh` rejects any testing text that contains the substring `no evidence` (also `no runtime evidence`, `no additional evidence`). Real runtime-verified evidence that describes an absence, such as "activity rows returned, with no evidence or lease columns", is classified as empty. `commit-and-pr` then stops with `runtime-verified requires non-empty testing evidence; PR body generation blocked.`

## Observed

Interactive full-loop for a managed project PR (private repo, placeholder). The `--testing` text was about 700 characters and described a rolled-back database transaction run. It was rejected only because of the phrase "no evidence or lease columns". Rewording to "omitting evidence and lease columns" passed.

## Expected

Disqualifying phrases should only match when the evidence text says that no testing evidence exists. Examples: the whole normalized text is a disqualifier, or the phrase is anchored at the start (`^no (runtime |additional )?evidence\b`). Descriptive evidence that mentions an absent field should pass.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh` (`_runtime_evidence_is_substantive`, about lines 464-482)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh`: add one case where descriptive evidence containing "no evidence columns" passes and a bare "no evidence" still fails.

title: dispatch-dedup-footprint: identical NEW wildcard scopes serialise disjoint batch issues across runners
body:
## Problem

Template-generated batch issues often declare the same glob-shaped Files Scope, for example:

```
### Files Scope

- NEW: `data/specs/lane-<name>-*.json`
- NEW: `data/log/*/*/*.jsonl`
```

Each batch creates only new files whose names are unique: a per-entity slug plus a timestamp, with leases issued disjointly by the project backend. `_footprint_find_overlap` in `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh` compares footprint entries as exact strings, so every such batch "overlaps" every other. Observed effect on a managed repo:

- Only one batch worker runs at a time. Pulse logs repeat `FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP (issue=#<other batch> files=…/*.jsonl, …/lane-<name>-*.json)` and then `blocked:footprint_overlap benign dispatch block`.
- An older batch issue lost every race to newer siblings for 4.5h. Its defer record (`_footprint_defer_record_overlap`) carried a ~6h TTL and wakes only on blocker lifecycle changes.

The current per-repo workaround is `footprint_low_info_paths` in `repos.json`, which treats `*.jsonl` and `lane-<name>-*.json` as low-information basenames. It lives in each runner's local `repos.json`, so every collaborator runner must configure it separately. Runners without it keep serialising the batches.

## Proposed fix

Choose one or both:

1. **Repo-committed opt-in.** Read extra low-information basenames from a committed repo file, such as an existing repo-level aidevops config if one is already consumed, merged with `repos.json` `footprint_low_info_paths`. All runners then share the setting.
2. **Wildcard NEW semantics.** When both the candidate entry and the in-flight entry are `NEW:` declarations containing `*`, treat the match as non-blocking. A shared wildcard pattern for newly created files does not identify a shared file. `EDIT:` entries and concrete paths keep current behaviour.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/repos-json-fields.md`

Reference pattern: `_footprint_repo_low_info_basenames` (repos.json opt-in) and the low-info skip in `_footprint_find_overlap`.

## Verification

- `test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh`: two issues sharing only a NEW wildcard entry (or a repo-committed low-info basename) do not overlap. Two issues sharing a concrete EDIT path still overlap. Existing test 17 (force-dispatch wakes but does not authorise overlap) still passes.
- ShellCheck is clean.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->

title: Reclaim regenerable build artefacts (target/, node_modules/, .next/) in idle linked worktrees
body:
## Problem

Worktree cleanup (`worktree-helper.sh clean`, `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh`) only removes worktrees whose branch is merged or safe to drop. Worktrees that must stay, because their PR is open, they have unpushed commits, or they're parked, keep their regenerable build output indefinitely.

Observed 2026-10-20 on one machine:

- Three Buzz worktrees with open upstream PRs held **~23 GB of Rust `target/`** (one held 18.8 GB across `target/` and `desktop/src-tauri/target/`), last touched ~10 weeks earlier. `cargo clean` reclaimed it with no loss.
- Each awardsapp worktree carries its own `node_modules` (~4.3 GiB with `nodeLinker: hoisted`) and `.next` (~0.9 GiB). Dozens of idle ones accumulate to tens of GB.
- The worktree base dir was 181 GB before manual cleanup.

## Proposed fix

Add a bounded, dry-run-by-default "idle worktree artefact reclaim" step for linked worktrees under the configured worktree base dir (`AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_BASE_DIR`):

- **Eligibility:** no live process cwd inside the worktree (reuse `worktree_removal_guard`'s cwd capture), no ownership claim by a live session, and no file outside the artefact dirs modified in N days (default 14, env-overridable).
- **Reclaim only regenerable, gitignored artefacts.** Use an allowlist: `target/` (Cargo, only when `Cargo.toml` is a sibling), `node_modules/`, `.next/`, `.turbo/`, `dist/`/`build/` only when gitignored, and `.hermit` caches. Confirm each path is ignored with `git check-ignore`, and never touch tracked or untracked-but-unignored files.
- Prefer native cleaners where present (`cargo clean`), otherwise move to trash. Log reclaimed bytes per worktree.
- Schedule it from the existing pulse preflight beside `system-cleanup.sh`, with a `--max-seconds` budget.
- Report it as a store in `storage-inventory-helper.sh`.

## Files

- New helper, modelled on `.agents/scripts/system-cleanup.sh` (dry-run default, `--force`, `--max-seconds`, batch trash)
- Guards: `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh` (`worktree_removal_guard`), ownership in `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh`
- Scheduler: the pulse preflight that calls `system-cleanup.sh` (`rg -n "system-cleanup" .agents/scripts/`)
- Inventory: `.agents/scripts/storage-inventory-helper.sh`

### Files Scope

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/worktree-artefact-reclaim.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/storage-inventory-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-storage-inventory-helper.sh`

Brief repaired: the existing inventory regression test must reflect the added store (20 to 21). This adjacent integration path is required by the already authorized inventory change. Run `AIDEVOPS_TEST_GIT_BIN=git bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-storage-inventory-helper.sh`, syntax checks and `git diff --check`. Preserve PR #35251 at its existing branch; continuation remains subject to signed revised-checkpoint approval and current lease guards. No destructive-action or security guarantee changes.

## Verification

- Dry run lists only gitignored allowlisted dirs in worktrees idle past the threshold, and skips any worktree with a live cwd holder or recent edits.
- `--force` on a fixture worktree removes `target/` and `node_modules/`, `git status --porcelain` is unchanged, and a rebuild works.

title: storage-inventory misses the largest stores (layout backups, isolated OpenCode DBs, tmp, worktrees) and never warns on growth
body:
## Problem

`storage-inventory-helper.sh status` is the framework's read-only view of disk use, but it omits the stores that actually grew largest. On 2026-10-20 one machine had `~/.aidevops` at **788 GB**, and the inventory reported none of these stores:

| Store | Observed | Tracked by |
|---|---|---|
| `.agent-workspace/work/repo-layout-migrations` | 490 GB | #35221 (retention) |
| `.agent-workspace/work/opencode-interactive/*/opencode/opencode.db` | 128 GB | #35222 (archive) |
| `.agent-workspace/tmp` (incl. a 74 GB `tui-capture-*`) | 120 GB | #35223, `system-cleanup.sh` |
| Worktree base dir (linked worktrees and build output) | 181 GB | worktree clean; artefacts: see the companion issue |
| `opencode.db.bak*` files in the OpenCode data dir | ~4 GB | none |

Several existing rows also report `sizing-timeout` (runtime-bundles, agent-backups, opencode-legacy, opencode-unclassified), and `observability` (11.7 GiB) is classified unknown.

Nothing warns when any of these crosses a threshold, so growth is found only when a user notices the disk.

## Proposed fix

- Add inventory records for the stores above, each naming its producer and retention owner (or "none" plus the tracking issue).
- Add a cheap top-level guard: a pulse-cycle (or daily) check comparing `~/.aidevops` and the worktree base with configurable soft limits. When exceeded, write one deduplicated advisory, not repeated comments, that names the largest stores and their `next_action`.
- Address the sizing timeouts by measuring large stores with `du -sk` at bounded depth, or by caching the last measurement with a timestamp.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/storage-inventory-helper.sh` (`_storage_emit_record`, `_storage_emit_retention_record` ~575, store list ~785)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-storage-inventory-helper.sh`
- Advisory routing precedent: `rg -n "advisor" .agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-status-lib.sh`

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/storage-inventory-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-storage-inventory-helper.sh`

## Verification

- `storage-inventory-helper.sh status` lists the new stores with sizes and owners and finishes within its time budget.
- With a temporarily lowered soft limit, exactly one advisory is produced, and none on the next run if nothing changed.
- Existing tests pass.
