title: record-included-release rejects Cloudron generated-catalog release tags
body:
## Observed

`full-loop-helper.sh record-published-release <PR> <TAG> <REPO> --generated-cloudron-catalog` accepts a Cloudron catalog release whose tag sits on the workflow's generated catalog-only commit (a direct child of the source PR's merge commit), and records `release:published`.

`full-loop-helper.sh record-included-release <FEATURE_PR> <SOURCE_PR> <TAG> <REPO> --workflow cloudron-catalog-publish.yml --event push` then fails for every earlier feature PR in the same release:

```
[ERROR] Tag v0.1.3 points at <catalog-commit>, not the merge commit <source-merge>
[ERROR] Cannot record release:superseded: source PR #16 release evidence for v0.1.3 does not verify
```

The source re-verification inside `record-included-release` uses the plain "tag == merge commit" rule and has no equivalent of `--generated-cloudron-catalog`, so feature PRs merged before a catalog release cannot be marked included.

Seen on a Cloudron community-app package repo (catalog workflow from `templates/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish-caller.yml` shape): source PR merged with a merge commit, workflow pushed `chore: publish Cloudron package X.Y.Z` + tag atomically on top.

## Expected

`record-included-release` accepts `--generated-cloudron-catalog` (or auto-detects a source receipt recorded with it) and re-verifies the source with the same catalog-only-commit and exact-source image/catalog attestation checks, then checks the feature merge commit is an ancestor of the tag.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` (command dispatch for `record-included-release`)
- the release-receipt module that implements `record-published-release --generated-cloudron-catalog` (reuse its verifier); exact file unknown — find with `rg -n 'generated-cloudron-catalog' .agents/scripts`

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle-commands.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-completion-evidence.sh`
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`

## Verification

On a catalog-published package: `record-published-release <src> vX.Y.Z <repo> --generated-cloudron-catalog` succeeds, then `record-included-release <earlier-pr> <src> vX.Y.Z <repo> --workflow cloudron-catalog-publish.yml --event push --generated-cloudron-catalog` records `release:superseded`; a tag whose parent is not the source merge, or a non-catalog-only commit, still fails closed.

body:
**Task ID:** `t18743` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Started:** 2026-10-20
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `feat` `interactive`

## Outcome

aidevops cleanup: on-demand storage cleanup command and r922 storage hygiene routine

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


- NEW: `.agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh` — orchestrator only; never deletes directly. Store table: name, sized paths, dry-run command, apply command. Bounded `du` via `timeout_sec`. Commands: `report` (default), `<store> [--apply]`, `all [--apply]`, `help`.
- EDIT: `aidevops.sh` `_main_dispatch_cleanup` — route no-args/`report`/store names/`all` to the helper; keep branch subcommands and help.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/routines/core-routines.sh` — add r922 entry + `describe_r922` (model: `describe_r913`).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh` — `setup_storage_hygiene` (model: `setup_opencode_db_archive`).
- EDIT: `setup.sh` — call `setup_storage_hygiene` in interactive and non-interactive scheduler paths.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh` `_routine_platform_owned` — `r922:storage-cleanup-helper.sh) name=storage-hygiene`.
- EDIT: docs — `.agents/workflows/worktree-cleanup.md` / `.agents/reference/routines.md` pointer to `aidevops cleanup`.

Out of scope (tracked separately): idle-worktree build artefact reclaim (#35242), storage-inventory coverage/advisories (#35243). The report names these gaps.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Add an on-demand storage cleanup entry point and a default scheduled routine so users never have to discover or wire up the individual cleaners themselves.

- `aidevops cleanup` (no args) prints a dry-run storage report: each aidevops-owned store, its size, and which existing cleaner owns it.
- `aidevops cleanup <tmp|worktrees|opencode|observability> [--apply]` and `aidevops cleanup all [--apply]` run the existing owning cleaners. Dry-run by default.
- New default core routine `r922 Storage hygiene` (daily) runs `storage-cleanup-helper.sh all --apply` through a dedicated launchd/systemd scheduler installed by `setup.sh`, registered as platform-owned in `pulse-routines.sh` so Pulse only runs it as a fallback.
- Existing `branches|remote-branches|local-branches` subcommands are unchanged.

## Why

Session evidence (2026-10-20): the aidevops workspace reached 788 GB and the linked-worktree base 118 GB+ before manual cleanup. The individual cleaners exist (`system-cleanup.sh`, `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh`, `opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh auto`, `observability-helper.sh retention-maintenance`) but there is no single on-demand entry point, `aidevops cleanup` only handles branches, and tmp cleanup only runs inside Pulse cycles (silently lost when Pulse is disabled).

## Acceptance

1. `aidevops cleanup` prints a dry-run report with sizes and owning cleaner, deletes nothing.
2. `aidevops cleanup tmp` runs `system-cleanup.sh --dry-run`; with `--apply` runs `--force`.
3. `aidevops cleanup all --apply` runs each store cleaner, continues past individual failures, and exits non-zero if any failed.
4. `aidevops cleanup branches --help` and `local-branches` behave as before.
5. `setup.sh` installs `sh.aidevops.storage-hygiene` (macOS) / `aidevops-storage-hygiene.timer` (Linux).
6. ShellCheck clean on all changed shell files.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh aidevops.sh .agents/scripts/routines/core-routines.sh .agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh

bash .agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh tmp
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-routines-selector.sh
```

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh
- aidevops.sh
- .agents/scripts/routines/core-routines.sh
- .agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh

title: worktree-recovery: prune approved cache roots from unmerged protected archives after retention (split from #35208)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up split from #35208 (approved in its maintainer review, decision table row "Cache-root pruning when the only extra blocker is `exact-commit-not-merged`"). The #35208 PR widens the approved regenerable-root list; this issue covers the separate, deletion-safety-sensitive change to **when** automatic maintenance may prune those roots from a protected mixed archive.

Today the cache-prune path only runs for archives whose terminal evidence is `commit == merged`, `open_pr == clear`, and `task == closed`. Legacy buckets for unmerged or abandoned branches therefore keep their `.venv`/`node_modules` bytes indefinitely, even though the roots are regenerable and the archive itself would stay.

## Approved scope (from the #35208 review)

- Relax only the `external.commit == "merged"`, `external.open_pr == clear`, and `external.task == "closed"` predicates, and only for the **cache-prune** path. Whole-archive candidacy rules stay unchanged.
- Keep every liveness predicate: `source_removal_outcome == "removed"`, `branch` starts with `refs/heads/`, and `worktree`/`registry`/`claim`/`process == clear`. An open PR (`open_pr == active`) must still block pruning.
- Require the retention period to have elapsed (`AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_RECOVERY_MAINTENANCE_RETENTION_DAYS`, default 7) so recently parked unmerged work restores without a reinstall. Use the same age evidence as `_worktree_recovery_maintenance_select_candidate`; unavailable age stays `unknown`, never eligible.
- The relaxation changes what an `aidevops.worktree-recovery-cache-prune-plan/v1` plan may authorise. Either version the plan (`v2`) or bind the retention-age evidence into each entry so existing `v1` plans keep their exact meaning. Apply must revalidate the bound evidence before any move.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-maintenance-helper.sh` — `_worktree_recovery_maintenance_collect_cache_roots` eligibility `jq` (the `.evidence.external.*` predicates) and its call site in `_worktree_recovery_maintenance_record_protected_entry`. Note: the classifier only reaches cache collection for entries whose primary reason is `archive-worktree-dirty`; confirm the downstream evidence is completed for unmerged commits in maintenance mode.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-apply-helper.sh` — `WORKTREE_RECOVERY_CACHE_PLAN_SCHEMA` and the cache-plan validator entry predicates (`$entry.evidence.external.commit == "merged"` … `$entry.reasons == ["approved-regenerable-cache-root"]`).
- `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md` — "Protected mixed archives". The file has a 500-line ratchet; reflow rather than grow.
- Reference pattern: the detached retention contract (`detached-within-retention` / `detached-head-published-retention-elapsed`) in `worktree-recovery-lifecycle-helper.sh` `_worktree_recovery_plan_classification_json`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-maintenance-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-apply-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-recovery-lifecycle-cache-retrofit.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-recovery-lifecycle.sh`

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-recovery-lifecycle.sh cache-retrofit` and the full suite pass.
- Add cases to `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-recovery-lifecycle-cache-retrofit.sh`: an unmerged mixed archive older than retention is `cache-pruned`; the same archive within retention, with an open PR, or with any live reference keeps its roots; a `v1` plan carrying an unmerged entry is rejected by apply.
- On an affected Linux host, maintenance reports `cache-pruned` for unmerged legacy buckets while archive commits and patches remain restorable.

title: release reconcile exits 1 on redundant lane ref-update 422 after terminal published state
body:
## Problem

`aidevops release reconcile <source-PR>` exited 1 after a fully published release. Its final output line was:

```
RELEASE_REMOTE_STATE=published
RELEASE_LANE_WRITE step=ref-update status=422 retryable=false
```

Yet the lane branch `aidevops/release-lane` already held the terminal state from the same run: `active:false`, `phase:terminal`, `terminal_receipt:"published"`, with `updated_at` matching the run. GitHub release, npm and Homebrew all showed the new version, and local deploy was on it. The 422 therefore came from a second, redundant lane write after the terminal write, which `_release_lane_write` (`.agents/scripts/release-lane-helper.sh:229-262`) maps to failure.

Observed on v3.39.52 (source PR #35249). The run was resuming a lane whose original executor had died during `remote-publication`.

## Impact

A release that succeeded reports exit 1. Operators and agents following `workflows/release.md` ("at most one documented recovery") may treat it as a terminal failure, or retry when nothing needs retrying.

## Proposed fix

- Find the second write in the reconcile terminal path. Make the terminal write idempotent: skip the write when the remote lane already equals the intended terminal state, apart from `updated_at`.
- Alternatively, on a non-retryable ref-update 422, re-read the remote lane. If it is already terminal for the same tag and `snapshot_sha`, report success instead of exit 1.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/release-lane-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-release-lane.sh`

## Verification

- `test-release-lane.sh`: a terminal-state reconcile whose second ref-update returns 422 while the remote lane is already terminal for the same tag exits 0. A 422 where the remote lane is not terminal still fails.
- ShellCheck is clean.

title: fix(secret-helper): secret get reports 'Secret not found' when gopass/gpg actually fails
body:
## Summary

`aidevops secret get NAME` reports `Secret not found: NAME` for **any** gopass/gpg failure, including failures where the secret definitely exists. The real error (pinentry/GPG/store) is discarded, so the operator is sent chasing the wrong problem.

## Reproduction (no secret values involved)

Normal path works — `aidevops secret get SOME_NAME` prints the value.

Now break gpg for one invocation (empty `GNUPGHOME`) so decryption cannot succeed:

```
$ GNUPGHOME=<empty-dir> gopass show -o aidevops/SOME_NAME 2>&1
gpg: public key decryption failed: No secret key
gpg: decryption failed: No secret key
❌ Decryption failed: exit status 2
$ echo $?
11
```

Same failure through the helper:

```
$ GNUPGHOME=<empty-dir> aidevops secret get SOME_NAME
[ERROR] Secret not found: SOME_NAME
$ echo $?
1
```

The secret exists; the message is false. During an ops session this sent us to re-check gopass store contents when the actual fault was gpg-side.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh`:

- `get_secret_value()` (line ~86): `gopass show -o "${GOPASS_PREFIX}/${name}" 2>/dev/null || true` — stderr is discarded and a non-zero exit is forced to success, so every failure collapses to empty output.
- `cmd_get()` (lines ~546-555): `if [[ -z "$value" ]]; then print_error "Secret not found: $name"` — the only failure branch, so it absorbs all of the above.

### Secondary (latent): name normalisation disagrees with `list`

- `cmd_get` line ~544 and `cmd_set` line ~480: `name=$(echo "$name" | tr '[:lower:]-' '[:upper:]_')`.
- `cmd_list` line ~570 emits **raw** gopass entry names.

`set`/`get` are symmetric with each other, so uppercase-only stores work today. But an entry created outside the helper with different case (e.g. `gopass insert aidevops/some_name`) will appear in `aidevops secret list` and then be unfetchable by `get`. Low priority, same file, worth fixing in the same PR.

## Expected behaviour

1. Secret genuinely absent → keep `Secret not found: NAME` (exit 1).
2. gopass/gpg/store failed → surface the captured stderr verbatim (it is diagnostic text, not secret material) plus a short hint (agent/pinentry/store), still exit 1.
3. Keep the existing contract: success prints the raw value to stdout only; all diagnostics to stderr.
4. Never print a secret value, even on the error path.

## Files

- Modify: `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh` (`get_secret_value`, `cmd_get`; optionally `cmd_set`/`cmd_list` for the normalisation issue)
- Deploy after merge: `setup.sh --non-interactive` (the deployed `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh` is overwritten by deploy, never edited directly)

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh` → 0 violations (ShellCheck 0.10.0).
- Repro case 2 above must no longer say `Secret not found`; it must show the gpg error text.
- Happy path still prints the value with no trailing newline change (`printf '%s'` contract preserved) — verify by piping to `sha256sum`, never by echoing.
- `aidevops secret get` with a name that does not exist still reports `Secret not found` with exit 1.
- `aidevops secret list`, `set`, and `run` remain unchanged.

## Context

Observed while rotating credentials during a monitoring/secret-rotation session; the misleading message cost a debugging detour before falling back to raw `gopass show -o`.

title: Bug: stale-recovery recheck ignores permission-trusted CONTRIBUTOR leases, leaving status:available issues stuck in claim_lock_failed
body:
## Observed

On a private managed project repo (aidevops v3.39.52, runner = private-org member whose issue comments carry `author_association=CONTRIBUTOR`), one issue entered a loop of `claim_lock_failed` after stale recovery:

- 22:55:59Z `DISPATCH_CLAIM ... max_age_s=1800` (runner A, device D)
- 22:56:35Z `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=ready ... expires_at=<~00:56Z>` (same runner/device/session)
- 23:25:58Z stale recovery (`_stale_recovery_apply`, GH#15060 tick 1/2): "dispatch claim 1710s old, last activity 1707s old (threshold=600s)", unassigned, relabelled `status:available`. No `CLAIM_RELEASED` and no `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=terminal` was posted.
- 23:27Z `no_work` skip-escalation posted (crash_type=no_work, fast-fail backoff 600s).
- 23:28Z two concurrent dispatch attempts (deterministic `dispatch_max` and supervisor LLM `--command dispatch`) both ran ~220s through every dedup layer and then failed at Layer 7: `ACTIVE_CLAIM: runner=A ts=22:55:59Z (1 total claims)` -> `claim lost ... another runner claimed first` -> `PRE_RUNTIME_FAILURE reason=claim_lock_failed`.

The issue stays `status:available` (and `priority:high`) but cannot be claimed until the ready lease expires about 2h after dispatch. Every pulse cycle in that window spends a full dispatch attempt on it.

## Root cause (verified in code)

The two readers of `dispatch-lease-claims.jq` disagree about who is trusted:

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh` `_fetch_claims()` (~L637-643) computes `_claim_permission_trusted_authors` and passes `--argjson permission_trusted_authors`, so a CONTRIBUTOR-association runner with write authority is trusted and its `ready` lease counts as an active claim (GH#34703 fix).
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh` `_stale_recovery_final_evidence_recheck()` (~L187-195) calls the same jq filter **without** `permission_trusted_authors`. `trusted_author()` in `dispatch-lease-claims.jq` (L1-5) therefore drops the claim, `any(.lease_phase == "ready")` is false, and the takeover proceeds although the lease is still valid.
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` (~L888, `lease_filter=dispatch-lease-claims.jq`) is a probable sibling caller with the same omission. Check it as well.

Verified the claim comment's `author_association` is `CONTRIBUTOR` via the REST comments API. `main` (origin) still has the same call at `dispatch-dedup-stale.sh:190-192`.

Consequences:
1. For private-org runners, stale recovery can supersede a valid `ready` lease. This is the GH#35218 symptom (silent release while the worker may still be running on another device) through a different path.
2. After recovery, the claim path still honours the lease. The issue is advertised `status:available` but is undispatchable until the lease expires, which produces repeated `claim_lock_failed` attempts.

## Expected

- All `dispatch-lease-claims.jq` callers use the same trust set. Pass `permission_trusted_authors` (from `_claim_permission_trusted_authors`, sourced from `dispatch-claim-helper.sh` or a shared helper) in `_stale_recovery_final_evidence_recheck` and in the `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` caller.
- When stale recovery does take over a claim whose lease is still `ready` (for example, the same device verified that the worker PID is gone), it posts a matching `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=terminal` or `CLAIM_RELEASED claim_id=<id> nonce=<nonce>` for that generation before relabelling `status:available`. Labels and the claim ledger then agree.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh` `_stale_recovery_final_evidence_recheck()` (~L176-203): pass trusted authors to the jq filter.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` around the `lease_filter` call (~L888-940): same.
- Reference pattern: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh` `_fetch_claims()` L637-651 and the regression test `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-lease-claims-private-member.sh`.

## Verification

- Extend `tests/test-dispatch-lease-claims-private-member.sh`, or add a stale-recheck case: a CONTRIBUTOR-association, write-authorized runner with a non-expired `ready` lease makes `_stale_recovery_final_evidence_recheck` return 1.
- `shellcheck` on the edited scripts.
- Production check: after deploy, no `status:available` issue whose latest claim has a non-expired `ready` lease without a terminal/release marker, and no repeated `claim_lock_failed` on the same issue in `pulse.log`.
<!-- aidevops:origin:worker -->

An interactive audit showed that unpatched trust stores on macOS, Ubuntu hosts, Docker images and Node runtimes all still trusted the compromised chain. Every aidevops user needs the same nudge.

## What

A new advisory file at `.agents/advisories/emudhra-ca-compromise-2026-10.advisory`. `setup.sh` deploys it to `~/.aidevops/advisories/` (`agent-deploy.sh:1330`). `aidevops-update-check.sh` `_check_advisories` then shows its first line in each session greeting until the user runs `aidevops security dismiss emudhra-ca-compromise-2026-10`.

## Why

The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CAs can be recovered from their public certificates. Browsers block them already, but CLI tools, language runtimes, containers and servers trust them until their CA bundles are updated. aidevops users run exactly those clients (curl, Node, Python, PHP/WordPress, Docker, Cloudron/Ubuntu hosts). Without an advisory, no session will prompt them to patch.

- [x] **Exact execution contract supplied?** New file; full content below.

- [x] **No stateful coordination to invent?**
- [x] **Focused verification and rollback are explicit?**
- [x] **No dispatch-path risk override?**

**Selected tier:** `tier:simple`

**Tier rationale:** One new static advisory file with its full content supplied, following an existing advisory → tier:simple.

## How

Create `.agents/advisories/emudhra-ca-compromise-2026-10.advisory` with exactly this content (no trailing blank lines):

```text
[SECURITY ADVISORY] eMudhra intermediate CA keys compromised — update CA trust stores (curl, Node, Python, PHP/WordPress, Docker, servers)

  Disclosed: 2026-10-20. Private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate CAs were
  generated so they can be recovered from the certificates. Anyone can mint
  certificates for any hostname that clients without Certificate Transparency
  enforcement (most CLIs, runtimes and servers) still trust. Browsers already
  block them.

  Test a client (a certificate error is the SAFE result):

    curl https://dv-g3b-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/
    node -e "require('https').get('https://dv-g3b-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/',()=>console.log('VULNERABLE')).on('error',()=>console.log('ok'))"

  Remediate:

             the OpenSSL store); /usr/bin/curl reads /etc/ssl/cert.pem, which
             Apple has not updated: see the workaround on the incident page
    Linux:   apt-get install --only-upgrade ca-certificates (Ubuntu 20260816*,
             Debian 20250419~deb12u2 / +deb13u1), Alpine 20261020-r0
    Docker:  rebuild images so they pick up the patched ca-certificates; official
             Node binaries ship a bundled store (fix pending upstream)
    Python:  certifi >= 2026.10.19, pip >= 26.2.2, uv >= 0.13.4
    Go:      1.27.3 / 1.26.10   Electron: 44.9.1 / 43.8.1 / 42.11.16
    WordPress: core bundles wp-includes/certificates/ca-bundle.crt; update core
             when a patched release ships

  Patched-version list: https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com

  Dismiss after patching and re-testing:

    aidevops security dismiss emudhra-ca-compromise-2026-10
```

title: Output scrubber misses DB URL userinfo and JSON name/value secret pairs (Cloudron addon logs)
body:
## What happened

In an OpenCode session, `cloudron logs --app <app>` printed Cloudron's addon setup lines, which contain credentials in two shapes. The OpenCode Bash output scrubber redacted one unrelated value in the same output but passed both of these through unredacted into the transcript:

1. A database URL with userinfo and a non-http scheme: `"value":"postgres://<user>:<password>@postgresql/<db>"`
2. JSON name/value pairs where the secret name is in a sibling field, not a `KEY=value` assignment: `{"name":"CLOUDRON_POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD","value":"<128 hex chars>"}` and `{"name":"CLOUDRON_MAIL_SMTP_PASSWORD","value":"<48 hex chars>"}`

Values are placeholders here. The real ones were in the local session transcript only.

## Expected

Both shapes are redacted before the output reaches the model or transcript.

## Suggested fix

- Redact userinfo passwords for any `scheme://user:pass@host` URL, not just http(s).
- In JSON, redact `"value"` when a sibling `"name"` (or `"key"`) matches the existing secret-name pattern.

## Verification

Add cases for both shapes to the existing credential-scrub tests and confirm a non-secret sibling such as `{"name":"CLOUDRON_POSTGRESQL_HOST","value":"postgresql"}` stays unredacted.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-output-scrub.mjs`
- `.agents/hooks/credential-transcript-scrub.py`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-credential-scrub.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-credential-transcript-scrub.sh`

title: t18747: storage: opt-in OpenCode session retention (prune sessions older than N days, keep all by default)
body:
## Task


Add an opt-in setting that permanently deletes OpenCode sessions older than N days and reclaims the disk space. The default stays **keep everything** (setting unset or `0`). When a user sets e.g. `storage.opencode_session_retention_days: 180`, the daily r922 Storage hygiene run (and `aidevops cleanup opencode --apply`) deletes sessions whose last update is older than 180 days from the active and archive OpenCode DBs, including isolated project DBs, then compacts the DB files so the space is actually returned.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Add an opt-in setting that permanently deletes OpenCode sessions older than N days and reclaims the disk space. The default stays **keep everything** (setting unset or `0`). When a user sets e.g. `storage.opencode_session_retention_days: 180`, the daily r922 Storage hygiene run (and `aidevops cleanup opencode --apply`) deletes sessions whose last update is older than 180 days from the active and archive OpenCode DBs, including isolated project DBs, then compacts the DB files so the space is actually returned.

## Why

Owner decision (2026-10-20, interactive session for GH#35245): "keep all by default, but maybe have a user configurable setting to prune after x days". Ref #35243 (storage inventory/advisories).

Evidence from this session, on one macOS install:
- `aidevops cleanup` reports the OpenCode store at 207.0 GB, by far the largest aidevops store (observability 11.8 GB).
- `opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh report` inventory: isolated DB `work/opencode-interactive/project-aidevops-*/opencode/opencode.db` is 79 GB active, `project-awardsapp-*` 34 GB active, `project-seoprostack-*` 3.6 GB; every isolated DB shows archive bytes `0`.
- `opencode-db-archive.sh` (daily archive via `opencode-db-archive-async-helper.sh archive-all`) moves sessions inactive 30+ days into `opencode-archive.db` but never deletes them, and its log shows almost every pass as `Archived N/N sessions (0 B freed)`: moving rows does not shrink the active file, and nothing ever shrinks the archive file.
- VACUUM in `opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh auto` is skipped for "low fragmentation", so today there is no path that returns OpenCode disk space at all.

So today there is no way for a user to cap this growth, even if they want to.

## How

1. **Setting** — add `opencode_session_retention_days` (integer, minimum 0, default 0 = keep forever) to the `storage` section of `.agents/configs/aidevops-config.schema.json`, next to `worktree_archive_retention_mode`. Document an env override `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS`. Read it with `config_get "storage.opencode_session_retention_days" "0"` as `.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh:240` does; treat invalid values as 0 (keep), so a bad setting never deletes anything.
2. **Prune command** — add `prune --older-than-days N [--dry-run|--apply]` to `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh` (it already owns the session schema, dependency-safe delete order at ~line 1174, live-session exclusion `_get_active_session_ids`-style logic, budgets and batching). Delete in batches from the archive DB first, then from the active DB for sessions past the cutoff that were never archived. Reuse the existing live-holder / active-session exclusions and `--max-duration-seconds` budget; never touch a session with an active worker or a DB with an active holder (protected skip, exit like the existing archive path).
3. **Space reclaim** — after a prune that deleted rows, VACUUM the archive DB (nothing reads it live), and VACUUM the active DB only under the existing idle-holder/stable-WAL checks (`_compact` logic near line 704). Report bytes before/after.
4. **Wiring** — call the prune from `opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh auto` only when the setting is > 0, so r922 and `aidevops cleanup opencode --apply` pick it up with no new scheduler. Make `aidevops cleanup opencode` (dry run, `_sc_dry_run_store` in `.agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh`) show either "Session retention: keep all (storage.opencode_session_retention_days=0)" or the count/bytes that would be pruned.
5. **Isolated DB coverage** — confirm `archive-all` actually archives isolated project DBs; the inventory above shows 0 archive bytes for all of them while the active files hold ~125 GB. If they are being skipped (e.g. protected skip because they are live), note why in the PR; prune must cover the same DB set as `archive-all`.
6. **Docs** — one line in `.agents/reference/configuration.md` and the storage section of `.agents/workflows/worktree-cleanup.md`: default keeps everything, how to set N, deletion is permanent.

## Acceptance

1. With no setting (or `0`), no OpenCode session is ever deleted; behaviour is unchanged.
2. With `storage.opencode_session_retention_days: N`, `aidevops cleanup opencode` previews the sessions/bytes older than N days, and `--apply` deletes them from active and archive DBs (default and isolated), skipping live sessions/holders.
3. After an apply that deleted rows, the archive DB file size is reduced (VACUUM), and the active DB is compacted when idle checks pass.
4. Invalid values (negative, non-numeric) are treated as keep-all and logged.
5. Sessions newer than N days and archived sessions newer than N days are untouched, and remain readable via `opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh sessions --include-archive`.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh .agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh .agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-maintenance.sh
OPENCODE_DB_PATH=<copy>/opencode.db bash .agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh prune --older-than-days 180 --dry-run
OPENCODE_DB_PATH=<copy>/opencode.db bash .agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh prune --older-than-days 180 --apply
bash .agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh opencode   # shows the retention line
```

## Files Scope

- .agents/configs/aidevops-config.schema.json
- .agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh
- .agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh
- .agents/reference/configuration.md
- .agents/workflows/worktree-cleanup.md

title: t18748: Parent: aidevops security tls-trust — data-driven client trust-store checks (local + fleet)
body:
## Task


A data-driven `aidevops security tls-trust` capability:

1. **Local:** probe each installed TLS client against a canary list of known-bad-chain test URLs, and report TRUSTED / REJECTED / UNKNOWN per client.
2. **Fleet (read-only, SSH):** the same probes on owned hosts, inside their running containers, and through the WordPress HTTP API of each inventoried site. Also report pending security updates for `ca-certificates`, including mirror lag.
3. **Advisory linkage:** an advisory file can name a check. `aidevops security` runs that check and auto-dismisses the advisory once every probed client rejects the canary.

The next CA/trust-store incident should need only a new canary line plus an advisory file, not new code.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `emudhra CA trust store fleet` → 1 hit — eMudhra response lessons (2026-10-21), folded into Context below

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-21
- **Session:** opencode:unknown-2026-10-21
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** During the eMudhra intermediate-CA compromise response, every exposure check had to be improvised by hand: the Mac's curl, Node and Python; 5 Ubuntu hosts; 92 containers; 17 WordPress installs. The maintainer approved making this a reusable `aidevops security` capability.

## What

A data-driven `aidevops security tls-trust` capability:

1. **Local:** probe each installed TLS client against a canary list of known-bad-chain test URLs, and report TRUSTED / REJECTED / UNKNOWN per client.
2. **Fleet (read-only, SSH):** the same probes on owned hosts, inside their running containers, and through the WordPress HTTP API of each inventoried site. Also report pending security updates for `ca-certificates`, including mirror lag.
3. **Advisory linkage:** an advisory file can name a check. `aidevops security` runs that check and auto-dismisses the advisory once every probed client rejects the canary.

The next CA/trust-store incident should need only a new canary line plus an advisory file, not new code.

## Why

`aidevops security` today covers posture, secret hygiene and npm supply chain. It has no check for client trust stores, host package security state, or container and app-bundled CA stores. Those were the whole attack surface in this incident, and nothing in the framework would have told users they were still exposed.

## Phases

- Phase 1 - local probe helper, canary config, `aidevops security tls-trust` wiring [auto-fire:on-prior-merge]
- Phase 2 - fleet probes over SSH (hosts, containers, WordPress, pending security updates) [auto-fire:on-prior-merge]
- Phase 3 - advisory → check linkage with auto-dismiss on verified clean

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/tls-trust-helper.sh`
- `.agents/configs/tls-trust-canaries.conf`
- `.agents/tools/security/tls-trust.md`
- `aidevops.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh`
- `.agents/advisories/emudhra-ca-compromise-2026-10.advisory`

## Context & Decisions (shared by all children)

Lessons observed on 2026-10-21; children must encode them:

- **Node:** Homebrew Node uses the Homebrew OpenSSL store, so it is fixed by `brew upgrade ca-certificates`. Official Node binaries and `node:*` Docker images use a compiled-in root store, so updating system `ca-certificates` does not fix them.
- **Node workaround:** `--use-openssl-ca` plus `SSL_CERT_FILE` fixes official Node. `--use-system-ca` does not: it adds the system store to the bundled roots.
- **Busybox:** `wget` results must be classed UNKNOWN, never TRUSTED/REJECTED.
- **Stores are per artifact:** each Docker container, WordPress install (`wp-includes/certificates/ca-bundle.crt`) and Electron app has its own CA store. Host patching does not cover them.
- **macOS curl:** `/usr/bin/curl` reads `/etc/ssl/cert.pem`, which Apple did not update; Homebrew curl is keg-only (`/opt/homebrew/opt/curl/bin/curl`).
- **Mirror lag:** the Hetzner Ubuntu mirror lagged the `ca-certificates` security update while `security.ubuntu.com` had it. Compare candidate versions against the upstream security pocket.
- **Shared hosting:** with no root, server-level PHP curl is outside the account's control. Report it as `host-controlled`, not as a fixable failure.
- **Hard boundaries:** probes are read-only. Never disable TLS verification to "work around" a failure. Fleet probes go only to inventory-listed hosts the user owns. Probe output carries no secrets.

- `aidevops.sh:1764` `_cmd_security` — subcommand dispatch and the no-arg full assessment

   - **`local [--canary ID] [--format text|json]`:** for each client present, probe each canary (or only `--canary ID`). Return one result per client/canary:
     - **curl clients:** `/usr/bin/curl`, `curl` on PATH, and keg-only Homebrew curl at `$(brew --prefix)/opt/curl/bin/curl` when present.
     - **Runtimes:** `node`, `python3` and `php` on PATH.
     - **Values:** `TRUSTED` (exposed), `REJECTED` (safe), `UNKNOWN` (network error, timeout or unsupported client). Busybox `wget` is always UNKNOWN.
     - **Exit codes:** 0 when no client is TRUSTED, 2 when any is TRUSTED, 1 on usage error.
   - **`probe-script`:** print a self-contained POSIX `sh` probe body. It takes a URL as `$1`, tries curl, then node, python3, wget, and prints exactly one line `<client> <TRUSTED|REJECTED|UNKNOWN>`. Phase 2 reuses it for remote hosts and containers. `local` must use the same per-client logic, so the two paths cannot drift.
   - **Classification:**
     - curl exit 60/35/51/77 → REJECTED; exit 0 (any HTTP status) → TRUSTED; others → UNKNOWN.
     - node error codes `UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY`, `CERT_*`, `SELF_SIGNED_*` → REJECTED; a response → TRUSTED; others → UNKNOWN.
     - python `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError` → REJECTED.
     - php `curl_errno` 60 → REJECTED.
     - Node probes must `process.exit()` in both callbacks, because keep-alive sockets otherwise hang the probe. Timeout: 15 s per probe.
   - **Remediation hint:** for each TRUSTED result, print the next action keyed by client. Examples: Homebrew Node → `brew upgrade ca-certificates node`; official Node → upgrade Node, or `--use-openssl-ca` plus `SSL_CERT_FILE`; `/usr/bin/curl` on macOS → see the canary's incident URL.
3. **Edit `aidevops.sh` `_cmd_security`.**
   - Add a case `tls-trust) shift || true; _dispatch_helper "tls-trust-helper.sh" "tls-trust-helper.sh" "${@:-local}" ;;`.
   - Add `tls-trust-helper.sh local || true` to the no-arg full assessment, after the supply-chain scan.
4. **New doc `.agents/tools/security/tls-trust.md`.** It holds usage, the canary file format, result semantics, and the parent's lessons list. Keep it short.

**Tier rationale:** The pattern and classification table are decided; the worker writes a new helper following `supply-chain-advisory-helper.sh` → tier:standard.

eval` and call `wp_remote_get(, ['timeout'=>15])`. `is_wp_error` with an SSL/certificate message → REJECTED; a response → TRUSTED. - If the `WP_HTTP_BLOCK_EXTERNAL`/`pre_http_request` short-circuit returns an error, report `BLOCKED-OUTBOUND` (neither safe nor exposed). - Also record the sha256 of `wp-includes/certificates/ca-bundle.crt`, so identical bundles are reported once. 5. **Shared-hosting PHP (no root).** Per PHP binary found at `/opt/alt/php*/usr/bin/php`, or `php` on PATH: - Probe raw `curl_init` with no `CURLOPT_CAINFO`, and the `file_get_contents` https stream. - Report `ini_get_all()` access levels for `curl.cainfo` and `openssl.cafile`. - When raw curl is TRUSTED and `curl.cainfo` access is `PHP_INI_SYSTEM` (4), classify as `HOST-CONTROLLED` with the hint "ask the host to update the system CA store". Do not report it as a fixable failure. - When streams are TRUSTED and `openssl.cafile` is `PHP_INI_PERDIR` (2), add the hint: per-site `.user.ini` `openssl.cafile=` fixes streams only. 6. **Output.** One row per target × layer (host, container image, wp-site, php-binary) × canary. <!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
# Unify automatic Pulse and manual dispatch under one managed worktree lifecycle

## What

Implement a common managed worker-launch contract for automatic Pulse and manual issue dispatch. Both entry points must register a worktree generation, reserve and bind a real managed process invocation, record completion evidence, and leave the existing archive/cleanup pipeline able to make a safe decision. Preserve their different task-selection and authorization policies. Deliver implementation, focused regression coverage and a bounded end-to-end demonstration; a design-only response is not completion.

## Session Origin and authority

User explicitly requested worker implementation on 2026-10-21 after independent design review. This supersedes the earlier deferred TODO status. No release, production worktree deletion, host-wide restart, or historical bulk migration is authorized by this issue. Existing operational cleanup is separate.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall for unified Pulse/manual lifecycle returned no relevant lessons.
- [x] Discovery: prework-discovery-helper.sh found merged archive work in 138481623 and existing manual dispatch changes; no related open PR returned. Open issue keyword searches found no matching implementation. Recheck remote HEAD and collisions before editing.
- [x] References verified: manual creation and launch in dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh; managed creation/reuse in pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh; reserve/bind in pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd.sh; registry states in worktree-managed-lifetime.py; archive_operation writer in worktree_lifetime_archive.py. Existing focused tests were discovered with git ls-files.
- [x] Tier: thinking — process admission, concurrent ownership, self-hosting dispatch and failure recovery require consequential coordination decisions.
- [x] Seeded draft PR skipped: this task has no implementation seed; workers must use the current maintained base.

## Evidence and problem

Automatic Pulse sets AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_MANAGER=pulse-cgroup-v1 when creating a NEW worktree, enrolls created state, reserves a systemd service, then bind-exec verifies the actual invocation before worker execution. Manual dispatch calls the same creation helper without selecting this mode, then starts headless run --detach through nohup. Observed manual records use owner-cgroup and can report owner-descendant-evidence-unavailable. This is incomplete evidence, not proof that a completed worker is still alive or safe to remove.

Both entry points generate feature/auto-DATE-ghISSUE. The name does not identify the real initiator. Existing Pulse reuse chooses the first branch-name match for an issue. Dirty staged/unstaged/untracked work and ahead commits are preserved; only clean verified zero-ahead preparation may reset to a trusted baseline. Preserve these protections.

## How — implementation contract

### Implementation Steps

1. Extract or reuse a common launcher rather than copying Pulse code into manual dispatch. Choose the backend before creating/enrolling a new generation. Keep task selection, auth/claims, model/runtime parameters, prompt delivery, environment, logging and CLI return semantics in compatible adapters.
2. Use the complete admission protocol: create/register -> reserve -> bind-exec/running -> verified quiescence -> sealed. Merely setting the manager environment variable is insufficient. Never silently fall back from managed admission to nohup/unmanaged execution after failure.
3. Distinguish worktree identity/generation from each execution attempt. Reuse existing generation and invocation identifiers where sufficient rather than introducing redundant IDs. Document whether sealing closes the lifetime; never reopen sealed admission by rewriting its state. Sequential resume must have an explicit safe contract.
4. Preserve append-only per-run provenance separately from current ownership. Record launcher/entrypoint, backend and a known trigger; automatic callers of the manual CLI must not be falsely attributed to a human. Use unknown where evidence is absent. Retry links/attempt numbers are independent of manual/scheduled trigger. Optional actor identity must have a trusted source. Never store credentials, full sensitive prompts or private host paths in public diagnostics.
5. Resolve managed reuse by exact repository/task/generation identity. Multiple candidates must produce an explicit ambiguity refusal, not first-match selection. Preserve safe handling of older branch-name records; no fabricated historical enrollment of owner-cgroup or legacy worktrees. Do not adopt active or unknown legacy sources automatically.
6. Keep existing directory paths unchanged. Specify a neutral future naming convention and compatibility strategy, but defer actual mass renaming or a broad naming migration. Neither directory names nor provenance grant deletion permission.
7. Preserve durable archive lookup: generation/source identity -> operation ID -> archive name/location -> verification/removal receipts. Reuse archive_operation rather than introducing a competing archive index. A basename alone is not unique; retain receipts after source deletion and keep archives self-describing. Legacy recovery journals remain valid and must not become invented managed histories.
8. Process quiescence must account for descendants, boot/invocation identity, unavailable observation and restart. Document that same-UID cgroup accounting is not a security sandbox against arbitrary hostile processes with equivalent OS privileges.

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` and the complete scope below; extract shared launch mechanics without duplicating Pulse policy.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-managed-lifetime.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_owner.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_archive.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifecycle_status.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-managed-lifetime.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-owner-lifetime.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py`
- `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-precreation-failure-skip.sh`
- `.agents/reference/worktree-registry.md`

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`, `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifecycle_status.py`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `.agents/scripts/worktree-managed-lifetime.py`, `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_owner.py`, `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_archive.py`.
- **Schemas/config:** Registry JSON and admission triggers in `.agents/scripts/worktree-managed-lifetime.py`; backend selection in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd.sh`.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** Repository `.agents/scripts/` is deployed by `setup.sh`; do not modify installed mirrors.
- **Migrations/backfills:** `.agents/scripts/worktree-managed-lifetime.py` must read historical records safely; no historical enrollment or bulk migration is authorized.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_archive.py` must preserve receipts and source data across rollback and interruption.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-managed-lifetime.py`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-owner-lifetime.py`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py`.

Callers are automatic dispatch and manual dispatch; creation writes ownership/lifetime registry records, reserve/bind/seal mutate the same SQLite lifecycle, status and cleanup read them, archive_operation records archive verification and removal. The listed tests cover dispatch, managed/owner lifetime and archive integration. The shared launcher extraction filename is not yet known: discover the narrowest existing reusable module and record any new required scope before editing. Search headless-runtime entry points for inherited environment, claim transfer and detach behavior before deciding whether a caller change is needed. Registry JSON and SQLite admission triggers are compatibility surfaces; use additive tolerant fields where possible. Deployed agents/runtime bundles are generated mirrors: edit repository sources only, not installed copies. No historical backfill, directory renaming, fleet deployment or release is part of this task. Cleanup/rollback must preserve original data and existing recovery journals.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Preserve transactional admission and exclusive ownership; systemd/filesystem side effects need recoverable handshakes.
- **Migration/rollback:** Do not fabricate historical enrollment; retain new records and archives on rollback.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Older readers must not mistake unknown metadata for safe completion; preserve existing CLI contracts.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Reconcile existing invocation identity before starting another worker; retain distinct attempts.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** Recover interrupted create/reserve/bind/exec/seal steps while preserving unknown or active sources.

SQLite transactions cannot atomically include filesystem creation or systemd calls. Specify recovery after creation-before-registration, reservation-before-unit-start, lost launch response, bind-before-exec failure and completion-before-receipt. Use idempotency and identity checks; unknown launch outcome must not permit a duplicate worker. Retain one finalization owner and distinguish launch accepted, process finished, task succeeded and source removed.

Handle simultaneous dispatch, live-owner refusal, owner transfer and archive/admission races. Preserve existing locks and sealed admission triggers. Recheck identity before destructive actions. Mixed old/new readers must fail closed without losing records; rollback cannot erase new provenance or interpret an unknown state as clear. Platforms without the managed backend need explicit compatible capability behavior, never hidden fallback. Existing legacy resume may be refused with actionable diagnostics until safe handling exists.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- **Surface mapping:** Dispatch shell tests cover both callers; managed/owner Python tests cover identity and admission; archive lifecycle tests cover preservation and durable receipts.

Run existing focused checks, extending them only to cover this change:

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-managed-lifetime.py
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-owner-lifetime.py
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py
git diff --check
```

Dispatch checks cover both entry-point contracts; lifecycle tests cover admission/identity/concurrency; archive tests protect preservation and receipts. Run ShellCheck on changed shell files and Python compilation on changed modules. Do not introduce a new runner or run broad repository gates without blast-radius evidence. In an isolated disposable repository, exercise both entry points with a harmless bounded worker under a real user systemd manager; record unit/invocation, lifecycle transitions, archive verification and removal receipts. Do not dispatch production issue work merely to obtain a test receipt. If systemd is unavailable, report that verification boundary explicitly and leave runtime acceptance open for a capable runner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Automatic and manual dispatch share the managed launcher, with compatible authorization, claims, runtime arguments and result semantics.
- [ ] New worktrees from both paths record trustworthy creation, per-run provenance and verified completion, without false human attribution or secrets.
- [ ] Competing admissions, unknown owners, remaining children, ambiguous reuse and sealed generations cannot start a second writer or permit unsafe cleanup.
- [ ] Partial failures and reboot/restart are recoverable without duplicate workers or deletion of unsaved work.
- [ ] Reuse preserves staged/unstaged/untracked changes and ahead commits; no historical enrollment is fabricated.
- [ ] Archive location and verification/removal receipts remain discoverable after source deletion; existing legacy readers remain safe.
- [ ] Both entry points pass focused tests and the bounded runtime lifecycle demonstration, with evidence attached to the PR.

## Recovery and delivery

After a logical increment, run the narrowest production-facing check and commit a recoverable checkpoint before lengthy gates. If a safety fuse stops verification, retain journals and source data, state remaining acceptance criteria, next safe route and resume condition; do not mark the task done. Use a linked worktree and a normal PR; no release or live cleanup. AUTO_MERGE preservation and expanded actor auditing are separate tasks, not reasons to weaken existing guards.

# Preserve and restore AUTO_MERGE in the unified compact worktree archive

## What

Extend the unified archive format to preserve AUTO_MERGE and its required Git objects, prove restoration without the original worktree, and allow existing verified retirement to proceed only for newly supported states. Measure added archive and shared-base storage. Do not reintroduce raw Git-administration copies or a second archive mode.

## Session Origin and authority

User requested worker implementation on 2026-10-21. This supersedes the deferred AUTO_MERGE TODO. Implement code and verification via PR; no production archive deletion, live recovery migration or release is authorized by this task. This leaf can proceed independently of launcher unification; coordinate if both workers need archive integration files.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall found no relevant AUTO_MERGE implementation lesson.
- [x] Discovery found the unified archive/compaction change at 138481623 and earlier Git-administration work; no matching open implementation issue or PR was identified. Recheck current remote HEAD before editing.
- [x] References verified: worktree_archive_state.py rejects unsupported administration/history; worktree_archive_* modules and existing archive lifecycle/shell tests exist. Trace their exact entry points before extending serialization.
- [x] Tier: thinking — preservation of Git objects, archive compatibility and destructive-retirement proof require careful correctness reasoning.
- [x] Seeded draft PR skipped: no implementation seed exists.

## Evidence and boundaries

Compaction retained real copies with git_admin:unknown_entry:AUTO_MERGE. AUTO_MERGE is a tree reference produced by Git's merge machinery, not proof of corruption or a still-running merge. An object hash alone is insufficient: unreferenced objects may be garbage-collected. Existing reflog-only/ORIG_HEAD history refusal is a separate preservation issue and must not be bypassed.

Support AUTO_MERGE itself first. A full resumable conflict additionally needs working files, conflict index stages, MERGE_HEAD and applicable merge metadata. Do not claim git merge --continue support merely because git diff AUTO_MERGE works. Preserve existing refusal for unsupported active-merge states. If complete merge-state support requires substantial new format scope, record that residual limitation and follow-up instead of silently discarding state.

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_state.py` and the complete scope below; add supported preservation rather than ignoring AUTO_MERGE.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.sh`

- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_state.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_administration.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_objects.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_snapshot.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_index.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_snapshot.py` and `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py` capture and consume archive state.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_administration.py`, `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_objects.py`, `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py`.
- **Schemas/config:** Archive metadata and policies in `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_index.py` and `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_administration.py`.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/`; never edit installed copies or runtime bundles.
- **Migrations/backfills:** `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py` must retain old-format readability; no bulk migration is authorized.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_objects.py` and existing retirement callers must preserve required objects and source data after interrupted verification.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-helper.sh`.

Capture/state validation reads linked Git administration and creates archive metadata/object references; restore consumes them; object storage and archive index govern durable bases and compatibility. Trace these modules and the existing lifecycle capture/verify/retire callers before editing, adding any genuinely required scope explicitly. Tests already cover archive lifecycle and CLI behavior; extend those, not a new harness. Installed scripts and runtime bundles are deployment mirrors and must not be edited. Existing archive manifests are migration/backward-compatibility readers: old archives must remain readable, and old readers must reject unsupported new required metadata rather than restore incompletely. No automatic backfill of existing archives or production source deletion is authorized.

## How — implementation contract

### Implementation Steps

1. Parse AUTO_MERGE using existing safe Git/admin validation; require a valid reference to an existing tree object. Reject symlinks, malformed content, unexpected types and missing objects with retained source and actionable reasons.
2. Preserve the referenced tree and its complete recursively required object closure. Reuse the existing durable object/base mechanism; retain reachable references sufficient to survive Git GC. Do not rely on the source worktree, a disposable object store or an unprotected object hash.
3. Record supported state in the single archive metadata contract and restore AUTO_MERGE in the target repository's correct Git administration, not in its working-file tree. Preserve integrity checks and deterministic verification.
4. Keep existing protections for reflog history, private refs, unsupported merge/rebase state, staged/unstaged/untracked content and object availability. Merely adding AUTO_MERGE to an ignored/allowed-name list is not implementation.
5. Report storage accounting separately for per-archive files, newly added durable base/object bytes and original source bytes. Do not promise a fixed size or omit shared-base growth. Avoid duplicating already durably preserved objects.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Keep capture consistency guards and atomic publication; changed source state must retain the source.
- **Migration/rollback:** Keep old archives readable and new archives intact on rollback; no destructive downgrade.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Version required metadata so unsupported old readers fail closed rather than restore incompletely.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Reuse durable operation journals and object identities; retries must not lose or duplicate required data.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** Retain source until independent restore verification succeeds; missing objects and corrupted metadata prohibit retirement.

Capture must handle concurrent changes using the existing identity/consistency guards; unsupported or changed state retains the source. Preserve transactional publish/verify/retire order and interrupted-operation resumability. Never remove a copy before independent restore verification succeeds. Design additive/versioned metadata with explicit old-reader failure behavior. Rollback leaves new archives and original sources intact; no destructive downgrade or archive conversion. Multiple archives sharing objects must not lose objects when another archive is pruned. Corrupt metadata and unavailable base objects must fail closed.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- **Surface mapping:** Archive lifecycle Python checks cover object closure, capture and independent restore; shell checks cover the existing CLI contract and rejection behavior.

```bash
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-helper.sh
git diff --check
```

Extend existing tests with a real text conflict yielding AUTO_MERGE and with representative large/binary content. Capture a supported state, restore with no access to the original worktree or its disposable object database, compare tree identity, working contents and git diff AUTO_MERGE. Use a disposable environment to exercise GC in the retained base and prove required objects survive. Verify malformed/missing/non-tree/symlink cases and unsupported full merge state retain sources. Check existing archives still restore. Compile changed Python modules and run scoped lint; no new runner or broad gate without evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Supported AUTO_MERGE state round-trips through the unified format without raw .git administration copies.
- [ ] Required objects remain recoverable independently of the original worktree and after applicable GC; shared-base retention/pruning is safe.
- [ ] Restore reproduces the AUTO_MERGE tree and git diff AUTO_MERGE; full merge continuation is not claimed unless separately verified with conflict index and merge metadata.
- [ ] Invalid, changing, unsupported or incomplete state cannot authorize retirement; existing reflog/history and process guards remain enforced.
- [ ] Existing archive compatibility checks pass, and new metadata has explicit safe behavior for older readers.
- [ ] PR includes actual archive/base byte measurements for representative cases and focused test evidence.

## Recovery and delivery

Commit a recoverable increment after focused verification, before broad gates. On safety stops retain source, archive and migration journals, list remaining criteria and a safer resume route. Deliver a normal PR without release, deployment or live cleanup. Do not merge launcher-unification changes into this leaf merely because it shares the overall storage objective.

title: Restore resumable interrupted merges from compact worktree archives
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
# Restore a resumable interrupted merge from a compact worktree archive

## What

Follow up #35296 by preserving the complete supported interrupted-merge state, not just AUTO_MERGE. Restore into an isolated worktree without the original source and prove the user can finish resolving conflicts and run git merge --continue. Preserve the single compact archive format and all retirement guards.

## Session Origin

User authorized worker implementation on 2026-10-21. Follow-up and blocked-by:#35296; wait for its merged object-preservation implementation before editing overlapping capture/restore code. This does NOT depend on implementing general historical reflog preservation. No release, fleet deployment or production recovery deletion is authorized here.

## Why

AUTO_MERGE alone restores a comparison tree but cannot reconstruct unmerged index entries, merge parents or merge messages. Claiming resumability without those would lose meaningful state. Necessary ORIG_HEAD and associated objects for this merge are in scope; preserving every older reflog entry is a separate feature and existing history guards remain active.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Existing review and source inspection identify AUTO_MERGE, conflict-index and merge-metadata gaps; no implemented full-merge support has been established.
- [x] Relevant capture/restore modules and existing tests were discovered with git ls-files. A fresh open-issue search was rate-limited; repeat collision discovery after cooldown before implementation, without bypassing the rate limiter.
- [x] Tier: thinking — Git state fidelity, compatibility and retirement safety are consequential.
- [x] Seeded draft PR skipped: implement after #35296 merges, not against a speculative seed.

## How

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_state.py` and the capture/object/restore modules listed below, building on #35296.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_git.py`

- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_filesystem.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_archive.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_migrate.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_retire.py`

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.sh`

- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_state.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_administration.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_objects.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_snapshot.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_index.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`

### Implementation Steps

1. Establish a supported merge-state matrix from installed Git behavior: HEAD, MERGE_HEAD (including parent ordering), merge message, relevant merge mode, AUTO_MERGE, required ORIG_HEAD, conflict index stages and actual working files. Discover optional metadata conservatively; unknown merge/rebase/sequencer states must retain the source. Document supported and unsupported cases.
2. Serialize conflict index entries structurally (path, file mode, object ID, stage 1/2/3; retain resolved stage-0 entries as appropriate), not as a raw copied Git index. Use binary-safe/path-safe encoding and Git-supported restoration mechanisms. Preserve partially resolved/staged files separately from unresolved stages and worktree content.
3. Preserve the complete required object closure and operation-related references independently of the original repository's disposable object store. Do not assume merge parents or an ORIG_HEAD object are reachable from archived HEAD. Reuse #35296's durable object retention/GC protections.
4. Restore metadata to the target's Git administration only after validation. Restore exact working files, index stages and operation state without executing hooks or automatically completing the merge. User-level continuation is an explicit verification step in a disposable repository.
5. Extend versioned metadata and validation so existing archives still restore and old readers fail closed on unsupported required state. Keep generation/source/operation/archive lookup and verification receipts traceable. Enable retirement only after independent restoration verifies the supported state.
6. Exercise content, add/add, modify/delete and representative rename or binary conflicts, partially resolved files, staged resolutions, ordinary untracked files and executable modes. Unsupported complex cases must be explicitly rejected rather than silently degraded. Treat symlinks, missing objects, malformed refs and path traversal as negative cases.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_snapshot.py`, `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py` and the existing archive lifecycle CLI.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_administration.py`, `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_objects.py`, `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py` write manifests, objects and restored index/admin state.
- **Schemas/config:** `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_index.py` and `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_administration.py` hold archive policy/metadata contracts; extend versioned data rather than introduce a second mode.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/`; edit repository sources, never installed mirrors.
- **Migrations/backfills:** `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py` must preserve older archive compatibility; no historical source enrollment or bulk conversion.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** Existing retirement callers consume verified archives; `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_state.py` must continue rejecting unsupported history. Retain journals/source on failure and do not downgrade existing archives destructively.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-helper.sh` are the existing harnesses to extend.

### Hazards and Compatibility

Compare final tree and parent identities with the expected merge; commit hashes may differ due to timestamps. Verify required objects survive applicable GC. Report archive bytes and incremental shared-base bytes separately. Use existing tests only, with focused additions; no new test framework.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A supported interrupted merge restores independently with matching working files, index stages, merge metadata and AUTO_MERGE comparison.
- [ ] git merge --continue succeeds after completing resolutions, producing the expected tree and parents.
- [ ] No raw Git-index/admin-copy archive mode is introduced; required objects survive GC and source loss.
- [ ] Unsupported history/operation state, corrupt metadata and incomplete capture never authorize source retirement.
- [ ] Older archives remain supported and required new metadata has safe mixed-version behavior.

title: Deploy and verify managed worktree lifecycle across approved Pulse hosts
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
# Deploy and verify the unified worktree lifecycle on approved Pulse hosts

## What

After the implementation dependencies merge, deploy the agreed lifecycle/archive improvements to the explicitly configured, operator-approved Pulse machines using existing update/deployment mechanisms. Verify actual creation, completion evidence, compact archive restoration and cleanup behavior per host. Produce a privacy-safe delivery report; a merged PR or matching version string alone is not rollout acceptance.

## Session Origin

User authorized this separate rollout task on 2026-10-21 and requested detailed dependencies. blocked-by:#35295,#35296,#35314: unified dispatch, AUTO_MERGE and resumable interrupted merge respectively. This is operational deployment authority for the configured approved scope, not authorization to publish a release, provision new hosts, use sudo, change credentials, kill active workers or delete unknown production worktrees.

## Why

Local deployment and verification do not establish that other Pulse machines use the same code or emit correct completion receipts. Running workers may use immutable older runtime bundles even after installed scripts update. Quota pressure and actual reclaimed bytes must be observed rather than inferred from successful service exits.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Existing session evidence includes a successful local setup.sh --stage agents deployment and guarded user-systemd cleanup; cross-host deployment has not been verified.
- [x] Repository setup.sh, lifecycle status/helper and recovery documentation are known integration points. Exact approved host inventory and remote runner access are not yet knowable from public repository evidence; inventory discovery is the first operational step.
- [x] Tier: thinking — cross-host authority, mixed versions, active-worker preservation and rollout rollback need careful judgment.
- [x] Seeded draft PR skipped: rollout consumes merged dependency revisions, not an unmerged implementation seed.

## How

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md` to document the verified deployment/rollback procedure and non-sensitive results; do not publish private hostnames, local paths or logs.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`

### Implementation Steps

1. Verify all dependency issues are complete and their PRs merged. Record exact source revisions and verify that the selected deployment contains all three changes. Do not deploy pending branch code fleet-wide.
2. Discover the existing approved Pulse host inventory and access methods from secure local configuration. Record local alias, platform, runtime, installation path, scheduler and capability status privately. Do not guess hosts or contact unapproved targets. Inaccessible hosts stay explicitly unverified; never call the whole fleet complete with missing evidence.
3. Establish a per-host baseline: installed revision/checksums, active runtime bundle revisions, live worker/claim state, lifecycle registry health, scheduler status, filesystem space AND user quota where available, recovery/worktree/archive sizes. Avoid dumping secrets or private task content.
4. Use existing deployment tooling and a linked source worktree where repository changes are necessary. Start with one approved canary. Preserve active workers and old bundles still in use; avoid restarting/terminating running workers merely to obtain a new revision. Verify new launches use the updated bundle while older runs retain safe handling.
5. On the canary exercise automatic and manual entry points using an isolated disposable repository and harmless bounded worker, not production tasks. Confirm generation/run/provenance, actual process identity, verified completion/sealing, archive location receipt, independent restoration and source removal. Exercise supported AUTO_MERGE and resumable merge using the dependency tests/fixtures.
6. Confirm the normal scheduled cleanup route invokes the installed maintenance path and emits durable outcomes. Measure before/after source bytes, incremental archive/base bytes and quota usage; report concurrent growth separately. Never lower age thresholds, bypass process/history guards or bulk-delete production sources as a rollout shortcut.
7. Roll out sequentially or in explicitly safe small batches only after canary acceptance. Stop rollout at the first reproducible regression, preserve evidence and use the existing rollback path without discarding newer archives/registry records. Report each host independently.
8. Document the reusable procedure and a redacted completion matrix. Keep full host mapping and detailed evidence in private operational storage, with references accessible to the operator. Any missing capability/credential requires a specific blocker, not guessed access or an unsafe fallback.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `setup.sh` deployment and `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifecycle_status.py` observation; approved remote invocation paths must be discovered from existing installation configuration before use.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `setup.sh` writes installed agents/runtime artifacts; existing managed launch/archive helpers write disposable validation records and receipts. Do not patch deployed files directly.
- **Schemas/config:** `.agents/scripts/worktree-managed-lifetime.py` and `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_archive.py` define dependency-owned registry/archive contracts; this task consumes them and does not invent another migration.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` produces installed script/runtime mirrors; verify exact revision or checksums and newly selected runtime bundle, not only CLI version.
- **Migrations/backfills:** Not applicable because this rollout consumes merged dependency migrations and explicitly forbids historical enrollment or bulk archive conversion; inspect `setup.sh` before invoking it on each platform.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** Existing `.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh` and `.agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-maintenance-helper.sh` remain the only production cleanup entry points; preserve active bundles and journals on rollback.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-managed-lifetime.py`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py`; run focused checks from the merged source on a capable canary.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Active workers may retain old bundles; coordinate rollout without killing writers or changing their generation/receipts.
- **Migration/rollback:** Preserve registry/archives across downgrade; a rollback that cannot read new metadata must fail closed and retain data.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Explicitly observe old and new workers during overlap; unsupported platform/backend stays unverified rather than silently falling back.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Repeated deployment must not duplicate workers or erase audit evidence; reuse host-specific checkpoints and verify source revision before retry.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** Stop further rollout after canary failure, retain working previous installation and all source data, record remaining hosts and the safe resume condition.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- **Surface mapping:** Dispatch and managed lifecycle tests exercise the new common launcher; archive lifecycle tests cover required restore contracts. Deployment checksums, systemd unit observations, registry receipts and quota measurements cover installed-runtime behavior beyond unit tests.

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-managed-lifetime.py
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py
git diff --check
```

Verify exact CLI options and deployment procedure on the merged dependencies before executing them; platform-specific commands and host aliases cannot safely be fixed without inventory. On Linux use read-only systemctl --user/journalctl observations and quota/df metrics. Use the existing platform-specific scheduler elsewhere; no universal systemd assumption. No new test framework, fleet-wide destructive test or release.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All dependency revisions are verified merged and included in the deployment source.
- [ ] Every approved target has a private evidence record and a clear verified/blocked status; no host is marked successful solely from a version string.
- [ ] Canary and subsequent capable hosts prove new-launch provenance, managed completion and archive/restore receipts through real bounded execution.
- [ ] Active/unknown sources and old running workers remain protected; no guard or age threshold is bypassed.
- [ ] Scheduled cleanup behavior and actual storage/quota outcomes are measured; concurrent growth is not misreported as failed deletion or reclaimed bytes.
- [ ] Rollback/resume procedure and privacy-safe host completion summary are delivered; inaccessible targets leave the objective open with specific blockers.

## Recovery and delivery

Keep private continuation checkpoints after each host and use existing bounded operational commands. A safety fuse stops the unsafe host path, not the entire objective; continue read-only diagnosis and preserve remaining criteria. Documentation changes use a linked worktree and normal PR. Deployment is authorized, release publication is not. Do not close the task until the approved fleet is verified or the operator explicitly narrows its scope.
