title: planning-publisher: task-regression guard refuses additive TODO.md publication (false deletions)
body:
## Observed (2026-10-21)

In a managed private project repo (name withheld), `planning-commit-helper.sh "plan: add t63 ..."` refused to publish from a fresh linked worktree that was based on current `origin/main`:

```
Refusing to publish: would delete or un-complete task lines not named in the publication: t001 t002 t001.1 t002 t45 t007 t013 ... t61 t001.
```

The change adds lines only:

- `git diff --stat origin/main -- TODO.md` → 2 insertions, 0 deletions.
- Running `_planning_publish_task_states`' own sed expression locally gives 59 checklist task lines on `origin/main:TODO.md` and 60 on the working file.
- `git rev-parse origin/main:TODO.md` equals the worktree index blob, so the snapshot was not stale.

The guard therefore compared against a merged blob that is missing almost every open task line. The workaround was a manual commit and PR via `gh_create_pr`.

## Likely areas

- `.agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh` `_planning_publish_guard_task_regression` (around line 597). Inspect how `merged_sha` in the resolved file is produced for this repo. Candidates:
  - the repo has no `.aidevops.json`, and its task counter lives on `main`, not `task-id-counter`;
  - a counter commit (`chore: claim t63`) landed on `main` between worktree creation and publish;
  - `TODO.md` contains an HTML-comment TOON block with task ids, duplicate ids (`t001` appears in both the Format example and Done), and very long lines (2586 chars).
- The `awk ... exit` lookup takes the first matching state, so duplicate ids such as the `t001` template line `[ ]` and the done `[x]` can also produce false un-complete reports. That would explain `t001`/`t002` appearing twice in the violation list.

## Expected

An additive TODO.md change based on the current default branch publishes, and the guard reports only real deletions or un-completions.

## Verification

Reproduce with a fixture TODO.md that contains duplicate ids (template plus done) and an HTML-comment block, with a counter-on-main repo. Run `planning-commit-helper.sh` with a one-line addition and expect success. A real deletion of an unnamed task must still be refused.

title: full-loop merge: stale refs/pull/N/head blocks prospective TODO validation (fallback only handles missing ref)
body:
## Observed

`full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <repo>` failed twice with only:

```
[ERROR] Merge blocked: unable to materialize pinned PR commits for prospective TODO validation
```

No fetch stderr was printed. Root cause: GitHub left the generated pull ref stale. REST `pulls/<N>.head.sha` reported the new head, but `git ls-remote origin refs/pull/<N>/head` still returned the previous head commit (about an hour after the push). In the same incident a CI run for that push stayed `in_progress` after every job had completed, so GitHub had not finished processing the `synchronize` event.

In `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-prospective.sh` `_merge_fetch_pinned_commit_objects` (isolated object-store branch), the fetch of `refs/pull/${pr_number}/head` succeeds. `rev-parse FETCH_HEAD` then returns the stale SHA, and `[[ "$fetched_sha" == "$head_sha" ]] || return 1` fails silently. The GH#34079 pinned-SHA fallback only runs when the ref is *missing* (`_merge_pull_ref_was_missing`), not when it is *stale*.

## Expected

When the pull-ref fetch succeeds but FETCH_HEAD != the REST-pinned head SHA, retry once by fetching the pinned object ID directly. This is the same guarded path as the missing-ref fallback: `_merge_is_pinned_object_id`, then a FETCH_HEAD equality check. If it still fails, print a specific diagnostic naming both SHAs instead of the generic "unable to materialize" error.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-prospective.sh` — `_merge_fetch_pinned_commit_objects`, the head-commit block after the `refs/pull/${pr_number}/head` fetch
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-planning.sh` — add a case next to the GH#34079 "absent pull ref falls back to the pinned head commit" case: point `refs/pull/42/head` at an older commit while the pinned head is reachable from another branch, and assert fallback plus no unrelated blob transfer

## Workaround used

Push a new commit to the PR branch (a merge from the base branch, no force-push). GitHub then regenerates `refs/pull/<N>/head`, and the merge helper proceeds.

## Verification

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-planning.sh` passes, including the new stale-ref case. ShellCheck is clean on the modified script.

title: Verify compact archives through canonical restoration before source retirement
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
# Verify compact archives through canonical restoration before retirement

## What

Make the production restore mechanism the basis of archive recoverability verification. For each new supported compact archive transaction, validate integrity/dependencies once, restore through the ordinary recovery worktree path, compare the required state, persist a bound verification receipt, and retire the original only while safety conditions remain valid. Eliminate unjustified repeated expensive checks within the same protected transaction without replacing real restore evidence with a generic verified boolean.

## Session Origin

User explicitly requested a detailed worker implementation task after inspecting actual code and timing logs. blocked-by:#35295,#35314: consume the unified managed lifecycle and complete merge-state archive contracts before modifying their shared paths. #35314 already depends on #35296. Coordinate with #35303 (default Git template branches-directory rejection); do not duplicate or undo its fix. This task authorizes implementation and isolated verification, not live deletion, release, host-wide restart or weakening legacy age/ownership rules. Fleet deployment remains #35298 and should wait for this improvement too.

## Why

Observed current code separates integrity/object checks from restoration. worktree_recovery_migrate.py returns archived for git-only before independent_restore; worktree_recovery_retire.py invokes verify_archive twice while planning and twice during retirement. worktree-archive-helper.sh verify validates artifact hashes and Git objects; worktree_archive_objects.py creates a temporary bare repository and worktree_archive_snapshot.py seed_base performs a local fetch of the recorded base. The ordinary restore path itself first calls verify_archive, then uses worktree_archive_restore.py and worktree-helper.sh to create a recovery worktree, applies staged/unstaged patches and restores untracked files. Therefore simply adding restore atop the current chain would add more verification, not remove duplication.

Existing read-only timing reports show median legacy capture around 0.8-1.0 seconds and individual archive integrity/object verification around 4.1-6.4 seconds across two measured repositories. Separate real-restore measurements were approximately 10.9 and 14.6 seconds, one sample each. These are historical, environment-specific observations, not a universal speed target or proof that fetch alone consumes that time. Nested timing stages overlap and must not be summed. Existing physical source fingerprint scans also repeat, including ignored dependency files; their cost must be measured separately. Keep all private repository identities and source paths out of public reports.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall for archive/restore duplicate verification found no relevant saved lesson.
- [x] Discovery found baseline changes 138481623 and 26e676c16 and related issues #35295, #35296, #35297, #35298 and #35303; no identical implementation task was found. Recheck current remote HEAD and in-flight PRs after dependencies finish.
- [x] Source paths, exact call flow and worktree_recovery_timing.py report command were inspected; existing archive tests are present.
- [x] Tier: thinking — admission, data preservation, filesystem concurrency and recovery-receipt validity are consequential design boundaries.
- [x] Seeded draft PR skipped: dependent work must land before this implementation begins.

## How

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.sh` and the scoped capture/restore/retirement modules below; reuse public restore semantics rather than create another divergent verifier.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_objects.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_snapshot.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_archive.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_migrate.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_producer.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_retire.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_retirement_transaction.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_migration_scratch.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_migration_state.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_timing.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`

### Implementation Steps

1. After dependencies merge, trace actual production capture, verify, restore, retirement and resume callers. Specify operation phases and the trust model. Distinguish artifact integrity, required Git-object availability, functional restoration, source stability and permission to delete; none is a substitute for the others. Preserve user-facing verify/restore command compatibility.
2. Refactor shared internal preparation so an ordinary public restore still verifies untrusted input, while the transaction can reuse its freshly verified, explicitly bound input without invoking the same heavyweight graph check again. Do not introduce a public skip-verification/force-delete switch or trust an arbitrary caller-supplied flag. Choose the narrowest internal contract, with evidence valid only for the protected operation and exact input identities.
3. Run the canonical restoration mechanism into a uniquely owned disposable worktree on the saved commit: import archived commits if required, apply staged.patch with index preservation, apply unstaged diff, restore ordinary untracked payloads, and restore all supported Git state from dependency tasks. Do not install node_modules, run a worker, claim a production issue or execute untrusted repository hooks. Use the normal creation/registration mechanism with explicit verification-purpose handling so the verifier does not accidentally block its own source-removal proof or leave orphaned lifecycle records.
4. Compare restored HEAD and required committed objects, index state, staged/unstaged results, tracked contents/modes/symlinks and untracked inventory/content. For supported conflict archives include stage entries, AUTO_MERGE tree and required merge metadata. Ignored cache files are deliberately outside the archive contract; their exclusion must not be mistaken for verification failure or permission to lose supported data. Test patch application failures and state mismatches, not just checksums.
5. Store a durable receipt tied to source generation/identity, operation ID, manifest/artifact digests, capture/schema/policy version, required base/object identity and verification result. Reuse existing archive_operation/migration journals rather than create competing authority. Preserve archive name/location linkage after deletion. A path/inode or verified=true alone is insufficient evidence of unchanged contents.
6. Before source retirement retain the relevant writer/admission checks, source identity/stability checks, archive/dependency availability checks, secure claim/rename and symlink-safe deletion. Document what each retained barrier protects. Advisory locks and private directories coordinate cooperative actors but cannot stop an already-open writer or arbitrary same-UID modification. Do not remove full source fingerprint checks until an equivalent concrete stability guarantee is established and tested.
7. Within one uninterrupted protected transaction, reuse the verified restoration result and prepared Git graph where safe. Across process restart, reboot, lock loss, source/archive/base changes or uncertain provenance, explicitly revalidate or redo the required work. Do not implement a persistent cross-operation verified cache in this first change. Unsupported or unverifiable states retain the source.
8. Clean up the verification worktree through an ownership-aware registered cleanup path, including Git worktree administration and registry state. Keep a durable cleanup receipt or recoverable pending state on interruption. Never recursively delete a path supplied solely by an archive manifest, and never leave verification copies outside bounded recovery accounting.
9. Instrument or reuse timings for integrity/object preparation, base import, canonical restore, comparison, source fingerprint, safety guards, verification-worktree cleanup and source removal. Preserve nesting/attempt identity; report non-overlapping totals, bytes and call counts. Compare a controlled baseline and revised path on identical disposable inputs. Do not claim speedup unless measured; a correctness improvement may legitimately change total cost.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_migrate.py`, `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_producer.py`, `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_archive.py` and existing status/cleanup consumers; trace any additional callers before modifying their contract.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py` creates verification worktrees through the shared helper; `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_retire.py` and `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_retirement_transaction.py` write plan/claim/removal journals; migration-state and lifetime-archive modules persist receipts.

- **Migrations/backfills:** `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_migrate.py` must recognize earlier journals lacking restoration evidence. Do not manufacture proof or bulk-convert production archives; resume conservatively and retain originals when required evidence is absent.

### Verification Before Dispatch


- [ ] Restart/resume and rollback have explicit conservative behavior, with recoverable owned scratch worktrees and no orphaned registrations.
- [ ] Source/archive/operation identity and receipts remain traceable after deletion; historical retirement is not counted as new reclaimed space.
- [ ] PR includes per-stage baseline/revised timing, sample sizes, bytes and verification evidence, with no unsupported performance claim.

title: terminal-blocker recovery: test fixture owner/repo#42 leaks into live queue and consumes pulse recovery budget
body:
## What

The live terminal-blocker recovery queue on a pulse runner contains a test fixture entry for `owner/repo#42`, enqueued at 2026-10-18T21:50:20Z with `reason=permission_required` and never cleaned up:

```
~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/terminal-blocker-recovery/queue/owner--repo--42.json
{"repo":"owner/repo","issue":42,"reason":"permission_required","opened_at":"2026-10-18T21:50:20Z"}
```

Each pulse, `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending` processes this entry, fails to resolve the placeholder repo and logs `blocker-recovery: incomplete stage=entry rc=2`. That marks the pass incomplete and spends the 45s budget, and the following `seed` stage then hits `rc=124`. Real entries such as `marcusquinn/aidevops#32446` and `#35194` share the same budget.

## Why

A test run that does not isolate the recovery root leaks into the real `~/.aidevops` state. The likely cause is a test that calls into `headless-runtime-failure.sh` with a `permission_required` fingerprint while `AIDEVOPS_BLOCKER_RECOVERY_DIR` or `HOME` still points at the real install. `_hrff_enqueue_blocker_recovery` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh:617`) then shells out to `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh enqueue`, and that falls back to `${HOME}/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/terminal-blocker-recovery` (`.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh:46`).

Candidate callers: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`. It uses `owner/repo` 42 throughout and sets `TEST_ROOT=$(mktemp -d)` at line 9, but only some subshells export `AIDEVOPS_BLOCKER_RECOVERY_DIR` (for example line 1242). `test-recovery-policy.sh` and `test-runner-capability.sh` also exercise this path. The exact leaking case is not confirmed.

## How

1. Find which test enqueues `owner/repo 42 permission_required` without isolation. Grep for `permission_required` and `_hrff_` callers in `.agents/scripts/tests/`.
2. Make the affected test file(s) export `AIDEVOPS_BLOCKER_RECOVERY_DIR="$TEST_ROOT/tbr"` (or set `HOME` to a temp dir) at file scope, before any helper is sourced.
3. Defence in depth (optional): `tbr_enqueue`/`pending` could reject or quarantine slugs that are not in `repos.json` and not `policy_remote`, so stray fixtures cannot reduce the live recovery budget.

## Acceptance

- Running the terminal-blocker, recovery-policy and runner-capability test files leaves no new files under the real `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/terminal-blocker-recovery/`.
- `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending` no longer reports `incomplete stage=entry` for placeholder slugs.
- ShellCheck is clean for the touched files.

## Local remediation

The pulse supervisor moved the stray fixture file into a quarantine directory under the agent workspace tmp. It was not deleted, so it can be inspected.
<!-- aidevops:origin:worker -->
### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-recovery-policy.sh`

# Restore a resumable interrupted merge from a compact worktree archive

## What

Follow up #35296 by preserving the complete supported interrupted-merge state, not just AUTO_MERGE. Restore into an isolated worktree without the original source and prove the user can finish resolving conflicts and run git merge --continue. Preserve the single compact archive format and all retirement guards.

## Session Origin

User authorized worker implementation on 2026-10-21. Follow-up and blocked-by:#35296; wait for its merged object-preservation implementation before editing overlapping capture/restore code. This does NOT depend on implementing general historical reflog preservation. No release, fleet deployment or production recovery deletion is authorized here.

## Why

AUTO_MERGE alone restores a comparison tree but cannot reconstruct unmerged index entries, merge parents or merge messages. Claiming resumability without those would lose meaningful state. Necessary ORIG_HEAD and associated objects for this merge are in scope; preserving every older reflog entry is a separate feature and existing history guards remain active.

## How

### Files to Modify

### Files Scope

### Implementation Steps

1. Discover optional metadata conservatively; unknown merge/rebase/sequencer states must retain the source. Document supported and unsupported cases.

3. Preserve the complete required object closure and operation-related references independently of the original repository's disposable object store. Do not assume merge parents or an ORIG_HEAD object are reachable from archived HEAD. Reuse #35296's durable object retention/GC protections.
4. Restore metadata to the target's Git administration only after validation. Restore exact working files, index stages and operation state without executing hooks or automatically completing the merge. User-level continuation is an explicit verification step in a disposable repository.
5. Extend versioned metadata and validation so existing archives still restore and old readers fail closed on unsupported required state. Keep generation/source/operation/archive lookup and verification receipts traceable. Enable retirement only after independent restoration verifies the supported state.
6. Exercise content, add/add, modify/delete and representative rename or binary conflicts, partially resolved files, staged resolutions, ordinary untracked files and executable modes. Unsupported complex cases must be explicitly rejected rather than silently degraded. Treat symlinks, missing objects, malformed refs and path traversal as negative cases.

- **Callers/readers:** `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_snapshot.py`, `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py` and the existing archive lifecycle CLI.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_administration.py`, `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_objects.py`, `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py` write manifests, objects and restored index/admin state.

- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-helper.sh` are the existing harnesses to extend.

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** A partially resolved merge can change during capture; retain existing writer/identity/consistency barriers and reject unstable state.

Compare final tree and parent identities with the expected merge; commit hashes may differ due to timestamps. Verify required objects survive applicable GC. title: fix: recover blocked checkpoints after fully released successor attempts
body:
## Outcome

Recover an exact blocked draft checkpoint after intervening worker attempts have themselves fully released, without bypassing ownership, revision, approval or fenced-lease guards.

This issue is being implemented by the interactive session. Scope is source repair and a PR for review only; no live guard installation, dispatch, merge or release is authorized. Security-sensitive authorization changes require review before delivery to the running framework.

## Observed failure and root cause

A preserved worker draft has an original authenticated ready attempt and blocked release. Later attempts each have their own claim, matching prelaunch/ready lease, release and closing terminal lease. A maintainer then corrects the brief and generates an approval for the exact original PR/head/ref/revision.

The current template accepts the original release and prints an approval, but validation still rejects every intervening attempt, including fully closed ones. Read-only evaluation reports original-release validity while successor-history validity is false. There is no basis to call those historical released attempts a currently live owner, but their comments cannot be deleted or silently ignored.

Owning path: `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh approval-template` -> `pr-checkpoint-revision.py:template`; claim and worker fencing use `pr-checkpoint-revision.py:candidate` -> `pr_checkpoint_events.py:successors_valid`. The latter permits only the original closing terminal or the exact new approval-bound claim/renewals. The template currently checks only the original release, not the successor-history condition.

## Reproducer

Use the existing offline fixture infrastructure in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-revision.py`; do not dispatch a live worker to reproduce this.

1. Start from `fixture()`: one authenticated original ready lease, its blocked release, and an approval binding the corrected issue and exact draft PR head/ref.
2. Before that approval, insert two sequential historical episodes, each with claim, matching prelaunch/ready leases, release, and matching terminal lease. Use one original runner and one different trusted runner; neither remains active.
3. On the base implementation, template generation still prints an approval, but `revision.validate` rejects it with `missing or ambiguous current revision approval` because the historical successor events are not recognized as closed.
4. In the candidate, run `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-revision.py ReleasedSuccessorTests`. The generated approval must explicitly bind both closed episodes and then validate. Removing that historical list, leaving an episode open, changing its identity, or introducing unrelated postapproval coordination must still reject it.

Before the predicate change, these new regression cases produced three errors and ten failed subcases; after the change they pass. The full existing revision suite now runs 19 tests successfully. This is a confirmed offline predicate reproduction, not evidence that a live continuation has succeeded.

## Files and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_events.py`: reference existing event parsing and strict postapproval fencing; preserve these primitives.
- `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_history.py`: isolate reconstruction of sequential, trusted, unedited, fully closed claim/ready/release/terminal episodes with matching runner/token/session/attempt identity. Reject overlap, interactive owners, mismatches, incomplete episodes and token reuse.
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-revision.py`: include the exact historical episode descriptors in a newly generated approval; rederive and compare them during validation. Legacy approvals must not silently authorize skipping history. Refuse unusable templates.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-revision.py`: extend existing pure predicates and mocked GitHub handoff coverage, not a new harness.
- `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`: document explicit historical approval, its limitations and unchanged ownership guarantees.

Preserve the existing current actor-permission check, brief hash, exact repository/issue/PR/head/ref/runner binding, structural issue link, hold labels, assignment checks, approval expiry and fresh fenced claim. A new unrelated event after approval still invalidates it even if it later releases. Closure or expiry alone never grants continuation authority. Do not edit published approvals or forge releases.

## Verification and acceptance

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-revision.py`: 19 tests passed in the candidate, including the existing handoff extended through historical approval, claim, ownership transfer, prelaunch renewal, ready transition, ownership verification and rollback.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`: exited 0.
- `bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed --base-ref HEAD^`: exited 0 on the staged follow-up, including changed-path Secretlint and Python annotation checks. Optional Markdownlint was unavailable; no claim that it ran.
- `python3 .agents/scripts/python-annotation-compat-check.py .agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_events.py .agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_history.py .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-revision.py .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-revision.py`: passed.

title: Report unsupported tracked permissions instead of generic worktree producer failure
body:
## Observed defect

On Linux, guarded removal of an otherwise clean linked verification worktree stopped with `producer:evidence-unavailable` / `compact-recovery-capture-failed`. The retained producer journal was in `capturing`, with an empty archive output directory. The source was preserved.

Read-only execution of the existing `git_snapshot` path exposed the specific failure:

`git_snapshot` -> `git_index_state` -> `supported_git_metadata` -> `supported_metadata` -> `ValueError` at `worktree_archive_filesystem.py:24`.

An aggregate metadata-only inspection found 13,021 tracked files at mode `0664`, 21 at `0775`, and 46 symlinks at `0777`, with zero hard-linked tracked files. The current policy accepts regular-file modes `0644` / `0755`, so ordinary group-writable checkout modes hit the intentional preservation boundary. No file contents or private paths are needed to reproduce this.

`worktree_recovery_migrate.archive_command` runs the archive CLI with `capture_output=True, check=True`. Its `CalledProcessError` reaches the broad handler in `worktree_recovery_producer.py`, which discards the specific reason and reports only `producer:evidence-unavailable`.

## Scoped implementation

Improve diagnostics without weakening archive/removal policy:

- Modify `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_producer.py` and, if necessary, `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_migrate.py` to classify the known unsupported-metadata failure into a stable, safe reason.
- Reference `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_filesystem.py:18-24` as the existing source of truth. Keep unsupported metadata fail-closed.
- Update the existing caller explanation in `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh` if needed so operators know that permissions or metadata require separate preservation, rather than repeatedly retrying an unavailable-evidence error.
- Never print raw captured stderr, traceback source lines, untracked filenames, file contents, credentials or local/private paths. Use a fixed allowlisted diagnostic code and fixed explanatory text.
- Do not chmod the source, remove group-write permission, clear ACLs/xattrs, rewrite the archive journal, bypass the guard, or delete retained artifacts to make the operation pass.
- Broader permission-preserving archive format support is outside this diagnostic fix and needs a separate design; do not silently broaden `supported_metadata`.

## Verification

Extend existing `.agents/scripts/tests/worktree_recovery_producer_cases.py` / `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-helper.sh` coverage using their established invocation patterns; do not add a runner. Exercise a disposable linked worktree with one tracked file set to `0664`, and the `0775` case. Confirm the removal path still refuses, preserves source bytes and modes, and now provides a specific sanitized diagnostic. Confirm unrelated subprocess failures retain a generic safe reason. Run the relevant existing checks and ShellCheck if shell code changes.

This issue authorizes the diagnostic implementation only. It does not authorize changes to unrelated project worktrees, permission normalization, deletion, or framework publication.

## What

PR CI's secretlint gate does not run the check that the patch-release preflight runs, so a PR can merge green and then block the next release.

## Evidence

- #35275 added synthetic DB connection-string fixtures and merged with green CI.
- `aidevops release patch 35323` then failed in `.agents/scripts/version-manager-preflight.sh` (`_run_secretlint_on_changed_files`) with 3 PostgreSQL/MongoDB connection-string findings in those fixtures. No tag was created. #35327 fixed the fixtures and v3.39.54 then published.

The repo-local `node_modules/.bin/secretlint` additionally flags `.agents/scripts/tests/test-credential-transcript-scrub.sh:166` (GitLab PAT rule), so the two runtimes give different results.

title: cloudron release preflight: docker manifest inspect rejects valid OCI index digests; use buildx imagetools
body:
## Problem

`cloudron_package_preflight_release` in `.agents/scripts/cloudron-package-release-lib.sh` checks each `FROM` source with `docker manifest inspect "$image"`. For some valid digest-pinned OCI image indexes, the legacy `docker manifest` command fails with `manifest verification failed for digest sha256:...`, even though the registry serves that digest and BuildKit builds from it. So release preflight fails on valid, immutable inputs.

## Evidence

- Image: `golang:1.27@sha256:820153096fda4de6ac1b7194d12e416b7dd8f4e9a33d17e0345b111b945162d8`
- `docker manifest inspect <image>` → `manifest verification failed for digest sha256:8201...`
- `docker buildx imagetools inspect <image> --format '{{json .Manifest.MediaType}}'` → `"application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json"` (resolves the same digest)
- An amd64 `docker build` that consumed this exact digest succeeded.
- Two independent headless workers, on two Cloudron package release PRs, hit the same failure and could not complete release preflight.

## Proposed fix

In `.agents/scripts/cloudron-package-release-lib.sh`, inside `cloudron_package_preflight_release`, resolve each source with `docker buildx imagetools inspect "$image" --format '{{json .Manifest.MediaType}}'`. Fall back to `docker manifest inspect` only when buildx is unavailable. Keep the requirement for a tag-and-digest reference. Also update any docs that mention `docker manifest inspect` for this preflight, under `.agents/tools/deployment/` or the Cloudron packaging/publishing skill docs (exact paths unknown: search with `rg 'manifest inspect' .agents`).

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/cloudron-package-release-lib.sh`
- Run `cloudron-package-helper.sh preflight-release vX.Y.Z` in a Cloudron package repo whose Dockerfile pins the image above. It must pass.
- Corrupt one hex character of a pinned digest. Preflight must fail with "Immutable Docker source is unavailable".

title: fix(pulse): worker-exit refill drains hold the instance lock for ~22 min and starve full cycles and scheduled routines
body:
## What

Stop worker-exit refill drains (`pulse-wrapper.sh --refill-only`) from starving full Pulse cycles, and with them every scheduled routine. Two parts:

1. Bound how long a refill-only run may hold the Pulse instance lock, and do not start a new drain straight after a failed one.
2. Evaluate due routines on a path that no long-running instance-lock holder can block.

## Why

Observed on one host on 2026-10-22, aidevops v3.39.55:

- Routines are evaluated only at the start of a full cycle (`evaluate_routines`, `pulse-wrapper.sh:1756`). A full cycle runs for about 28 minutes on this host.
- `_pulse_run_refill_only` (`pulse-event-refill.sh:363`) takes the same instance lock and holds it for an entire `apply_dispatch_max`. One drain ran from 03:26 to 03:48 UTC and then logged `action=drain_failed source=worker-exit pass=1 trigger=retained`, because `Dispatch_max skipped before candidate enumeration: cycle wall-clock budget below dispatch reserve (remaining=316s floor=600s ...)`. It dispatched nothing. At 03:49 a pass-2 wake took the lock again. Meanwhile every launchd start (`StartInterval` 120 s) logged `another instance running (PID <refill pid>, age Ns), skipping`.
- Effect: a script routine on `cron(15,45 * * * *)` ran 17 times in about 11.6 h against roughly 23 slots (gaps of 4,378 s, 5,085 s and 5,527 s between runs). Its last run was at about 02:44 UTC, and the 03:15 and 03:45 slots were both missed. That routine refills a project's work queue, so a missed slot leaves workers idle.
- Searching closed issues (#32546, #32688, #33113, #33560, #34018) found no fix for refill drains holding the lock and starving routines.

## How

- In `_pulse_run_refill_only` / `pulse_event_refill_drain` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh:303-394`), give the refill-only run a wall-clock budget, for example `PULSE_EVENT_REFILL_MAX_SECONDS` (default 300). Make `apply_dispatch_max` honour it through the existing cycle-budget variables, so the run stops admitting candidates once the budget is spent.
- After `drain_failed ... trigger=retained`, record a cooldown (for example a timestamp file beside the trigger). A worker-exit refill inside the cooldown should exit with `action=deferred reason=failed_drain_cooldown trigger=retained` instead of taking the lock. The next full cycle's `cycle-final` drain still consumes the retained trigger.
- Routine evaluation: run `evaluate_routines` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh:1133`) under its own lock rather than only inside the full cycle. Two acceptable options:
  - (a) Before `_pulse_event_refill_wait_for_instance_lock`, refill-only runs (and full-cycle starts that lose the lock) invoke a routines-only pass guarded by a dedicated `routines.lockdir`.
  - (b) Add a `--routines-only` mode modelled on `--merge-only` (jitter skip at `pulse-wrapper.sh:171-185`; scheduler install in `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh`), run every 60-120 s.

  Script routines already use per-routine runner locks (`_routine_acquire_runner_lock`, `pulse-routines.sh:538`), so overlapping evaluators cannot double-start a routine. Keep the REST budget gate (`_pulse_run_budget_priority_stage_with_timeout`) around the new call.
- Keep the in-cycle `evaluate_routines` call at line 1756. It becomes a backstop, and `last_run_epoch` state stops a routine running twice.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-routine-standalone.sh`

## Acceptance

- A refill-only run releases the instance lock within `PULSE_EVENT_REFILL_MAX_SECONDS` plus one candidate's stage timeout. Its log shows `action=drain_completed` or `action=drain_budget_exhausted ... trigger=retained`, never a hold longer than about 22 minutes.
- After a `drain_failed`, a worker-exit refill inside the cooldown does not take the instance lock, and the next full cycle starts on its normal launchd tick.
- With the instance lock held by a long-running process, a script routine due at `:15` starts within 2 minutes of `:15`: `routine <id> is due` and `dispatching script` appear in `pulse.log`. A test covers this, or extend `test-pulse-merge-routine-standalone.sh`.
- A routine is never started twice for one due slot, either across evaluators or across hosts sharing state.
- `shellcheck` reports zero violations on every edited script, and the existing pulse tests pass.

title: Bug: terminal-blocker recovery drops own circuits when runner association is CONTRIBUTOR (self login not passed to trusted-comment fetch)
body:
## Observed

On a runner whose GitHub association in a managed private repo is `CONTRIBUTOR` (write access through an org team, not a direct collaborator), `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending` never surfaces any of that runner's own terminal-blocker circuits. The AI brief owner never sees them, and the issues stay `status:blocked`.

Evidence from one pulse sweep (2026-10-22, aidevops v3.39.5x):

- `seed` enqueued 30 entries for one managed private repo (`<private-repo>`). Each had a `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_CIRCUIT active=true` comment posted by this runner, for example reason `permission_required`.
- `pending` printed nothing for any of them. Running the stage directly (`terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh _stage _tbr_check_entry <queue-file>` with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_SELF_LOGIN=<runner>`) exited 1 and deleted the queue file. The issue labels did not change: it stayed `status:blocked`.
- A `bash -x` trace shows that `terminal_blocker_fetch_trusted_comments` ran `jq --arg self ''`. The runner's own circuit comments, with association `CONTRIBUTOR`, were dropped as untrusted.
- The next `seed` re-enqueues the same issues, because seed resolves `self` itself. The loop repeats on every sweep.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh:452` (`_tbr_check_entry`):

```bash
comments=$(terminal_blocker_fetch_trusted_comments "$issue" "$repo") || return 2
```

`terminal_blocker_fetch_trusted_comments` (`.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh:388`) reads the self login **only from its optional `$3` argument**. It does not read `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_SELF_LOGIN`. `tbr_pending` resolves and exports `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_SELF_LOGIN` (lines 512-517), but `_tbr_check_entry` never passes it. As a result:

1. The runner's own circuit is filtered out, so `terminal_blocker_circuit_active` returns false.
2. `terminal_blocker_observation_hold_active` returns 1, which is treated as "re-armed".
3. `_tbr_release_circuit_hold` gets the same filtered comments, finds no circuit evidence, and returns without relabelling.
4. The queue entry and its decision are deleted (`rm -f "$file" ...`), so the hold is never shown to the owner.

Repos where the runner is `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR` are unaffected, which is why the aidevops entries still surface.

## Fix

In `_tbr_check_entry`, pass the resolved login:

```bash
comments=$(terminal_blocker_fetch_trusted_comments "$issue" "$repo" "${TERMINAL_BLOCKER_SELF_LOGIN:-}") || return 2
```

Also check the other callers of `terminal_blocker_fetch_trusted_comments`, for example `rg -n "terminal_blocker_fetch_trusted_comments" .agents/scripts/`, for the same missing third argument.

Secondary, same file: `TBR_STAGE_SECONDS=8` (line 53) caps the whole `seed` stage, including one paginated comments read per candidate across every pulse repo. With the defaults, seed timed out (`rc=124`) on every run, and the queue only filled when `BLOCKER_RECOVERY_STAGE_SECONDS=400` was set. Consider a separate, larger seed stage cap, or count per-issue progress as completion.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- Extend the existing terminal-blocker recovery test (`rg -l "terminal-blocker-recovery-helper" .agents/scripts/tests/`). Add a fixture in which the runner's circuit comment has `author_association: CONTRIBUTOR` and `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_SELF_LOGIN` matches its author. `pending` must print the entry and keep the queue file. Today it deletes the file and prints nothing.
- On a live runner: `env BLOCKER_RECOVERY_STAGE_SECONDS=400 BLOCKER_RECOVERY_BUDGET_SECONDS=900 terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending` prints JSON lines for the queued own-circuit entries.

# Deploy and verify the unified worktree lifecycle on approved Pulse hosts

## What

After the implementation dependencies merge, deploy the agreed lifecycle/archive improvements to the explicitly configured, operator-approved Pulse machines using existing update/deployment mechanisms. Verify actual creation, completion evidence, compact archive restoration and cleanup behavior per host. Produce a privacy-safe delivery report; a merged PR or matching version string alone is not rollout acceptance.

## Session Origin

User authorized this separate rollout task on 2026-10-21 and requested detailed dependencies. blocked-by:#35295,#35296,#35314: unified dispatch, AUTO_MERGE and resumable interrupted merge respectively. This is operational deployment authority for the configured approved scope, not authorization to publish a release, provision new hosts, use sudo, change credentials, kill active workers or delete unknown production worktrees.

## Why

Local deployment and verification do not establish that other Pulse machines use the same code or emit correct completion receipts. Running workers may use immutable older runtime bundles even after installed scripts update. Quota pressure and actual reclaimed bytes must be observed rather than inferred from successful service exits.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Existing session evidence includes a successful local setup.sh --stage agents deployment and guarded user-systemd cleanup; cross-host deployment has not been verified.
- [x] Repository setup.sh, lifecycle status/helper and recovery documentation are known integration points. Exact approved host inventory and remote runner access are not yet knowable from public repository evidence; inventory discovery is the first operational step.
- [x] Tier: thinking — cross-host authority, mixed versions, active-worker preservation and rollout rollback need careful judgment.
- [x] Seeded draft PR skipped: rollout consumes merged dependency revisions, not an unmerged implementation seed.

## How

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md` to document the verified deployment/rollback procedure and non-sensitive results; do not publish private hostnames, local paths or logs.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`

### Implementation Steps

1. Verify all dependency issues are complete and their PRs merged. Record exact source revisions and verify that the selected deployment contains all three changes. Do not deploy pending branch code fleet-wide.
2. Discover the existing approved Pulse host inventory and access methods from secure local configuration. Record local alias, platform, runtime, installation path, scheduler and capability status privately. Do not guess hosts or contact unapproved targets. Inaccessible hosts stay explicitly unverified; never call the whole fleet complete with missing evidence.
3. Establish a per-host baseline: installed revision/checksums, active runtime bundle revisions, live worker/claim state, lifecycle registry health, scheduler status, filesystem space AND user quota where available, recovery/worktree/archive sizes. Avoid dumping secrets or private task content.
4. Use existing deployment tooling and a linked source worktree where repository changes are necessary. Start with one approved canary. Preserve active workers and old bundles still in use; avoid restarting/terminating running workers merely to obtain a new revision. Verify new launches use the updated bundle while older runs retain safe handling.
5. On the canary exercise automatic and manual entry points using an isolated disposable repository and harmless bounded worker, not production tasks. Confirm generation/run/provenance, actual process identity, verified completion/sealing, archive location receipt, independent restoration and source removal. Exercise supported AUTO_MERGE and resumable merge using the dependency tests/fixtures.
6. Confirm the normal scheduled cleanup route invokes the installed maintenance path and emits durable outcomes. Measure before/after source bytes, incremental archive/base bytes and quota usage; report concurrent growth separately. Never lower age thresholds, bypass process/history guards or bulk-delete production sources as a rollout shortcut.
7. Roll out sequentially or in explicitly safe small batches only after canary acceptance. Stop rollout at the first reproducible regression, preserve evidence and use the existing rollback path without discarding newer archives/registry records. Report each host independently.
8. Document the reusable procedure and a redacted completion matrix. Keep full host mapping and detailed evidence in private operational storage, with references accessible to the operator. Any missing capability/credential requires a specific blocker, not guessed access or an unsafe fallback.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `setup.sh` deployment and `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifecycle_status.py` observation; approved remote invocation paths must be discovered from existing installation configuration before use.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `setup.sh` writes installed agents/runtime artifacts; existing managed launch/archive helpers write disposable validation records and receipts. Do not patch deployed files directly.
- **Schemas/config:** `.agents/scripts/worktree-managed-lifetime.py` and `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_archive.py` define dependency-owned registry/archive contracts; this task consumes them and does not invent another migration.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` produces installed script/runtime mirrors; verify exact revision or checksums and newly selected runtime bundle, not only CLI version.
- **Migrations/backfills:** Not applicable because this rollout consumes merged dependency migrations and explicitly forbids historical enrollment or bulk archive conversion; inspect `setup.sh` before invoking it on each platform.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** Existing `.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh` and `.agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-maintenance-helper.sh` remain the only production cleanup entry points; preserve active bundles and journals on rollback.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-managed-lifetime.py`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py`; run focused checks from the merged source on a capable canary.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Active workers may retain old bundles; coordinate rollout without killing writers or changing their generation/receipts.
- **Migration/rollback:** Preserve registry/archives across downgrade; a rollback that cannot read new metadata must fail closed and retain data.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Explicitly observe old and new workers during overlap; unsupported platform/backend stays unverified rather than silently falling back.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Repeated deployment must not duplicate workers or erase audit evidence; reuse host-specific checkpoints and verify source revision before retry.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** Stop further rollout after canary failure, retain working previous installation and all source data, record remaining hosts and the safe resume condition.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- **Surface mapping:** Dispatch and managed lifecycle tests exercise the new common launcher; archive lifecycle tests cover required restore contracts. Deployment checksums, systemd unit observations, registry receipts and quota measurements cover installed-runtime behavior beyond unit tests.

```bash

python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-managed-lifetime.py
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py
git diff --check
```

Verify exact CLI options and deployment procedure on the merged dependencies before executing them; platform-specific commands and host aliases cannot safely be fixed without inventory. On Linux use read-only systemctl --user/journalctl observations and quota/df metrics. Use the existing platform-specific scheduler elsewhere; no universal systemd assumption. No new test framework, fleet-wide destructive test or release.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All dependency revisions are verified merged and included in the deployment source.
- [ ] Every approved target has a private evidence record and a clear verified/blocked status; no host is marked successful solely from a version string.
- [ ] Canary and subsequent capable hosts prove new-launch provenance, managed completion and archive/restore receipts through real bounded execution.
- [ ] Active/unknown sources and old running workers remain protected; no guard or age threshold is bypassed.
- [ ] Scheduled cleanup behavior and actual storage/quota outcomes are measured; concurrent growth is not misreported as failed deletion or reclaimed bytes.
- [ ] Rollback/resume procedure and privacy-safe host completion summary are delivered; inaccessible targets leave the objective open with specific blockers.

## Recovery and delivery

Keep private continuation checkpoints after each host and use existing bounded operational commands. A safety fuse stops the unsafe host path, not the entire objective; continue read-only diagnosis and preserve remaining criteria. Documentation changes use a linked worktree and normal PR. Deployment is authorized, release publication is not. Do not close the task until the approved fleet is verified or the operator explicitly narrows its scope.

title: Bug: stale_assignment_reset release leaves worker draft checkpoint permanently undispatchable
body:
## What

A worker draft checkpoint PR becomes permanently undispatchable after the pulse
stale-assignment reset releases its linked issue. Ordinary redispatch is blocked
by the draft-checkpoint dedup, and stalled-checkpoint continuation refuses
because the release reason `stale_assignment_reset` is not a recognised stall
release.

## Observed (daily pulse sweep, 2026-10-22, managed private repo)

- Linked issue: open, `status:available`, `auto-dispatch`, unassigned.
- Draft PR authored by runner A (PR-author binding), last commit 2026-10-21 ~18:42Z.
- Runner B claimed the issue at 09:16Z (`DISPATCH_CLAIM` + prelaunch `DISPATCH_LEASE`),
  produced no commits, and at 11:31Z posted
  `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=stale_assignment_reset` (from
  `pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh:_normalize_stale_post_release`), unassigning
  and setting `status:available`.
- Ordinary dispatch on runner A's pulse:
  `Dedup: draft PR #<pr> is a durable checkpoint for issue #<issue>; ordinary redispatch is blocked`
  → `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=dedup_active_claim`.
- Continuation path on runner A:
  `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh dispatch-stalled <repo> <path> <issue> <pr> <runner-A>`
  → `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_SKIPPED: PR #<pr> ... has no current stall release`.

Result: the issue is labelled available but no runner can resume it; the
objective is ownerless with no wake condition.

## Root cause (hypothesis, verified by reading code)

`.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:45` defines
`_PCC_STALL_RELEASE_PATTERN='^(no_activity|wall_clock_stale|watchdog_kill:...|[a-z0-9_]*_stall|[a-z0-9_]*timeout[a-z0-9_]*)$'`.
`stale_assignment_reset` (written by `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh:74`)
matches none of these alternatives, so `_pcc_stall_release_evidence`
(`pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:737`) returns 1 and
`_pcc_dispatch_stalled` (`:855`) skips. GH#33997 fixed the assigned-draft case;
this is the unassigned-after-stale-reset case, especially across runners where
the resetting runner is not the PR author.

## How

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:45` — treat
  `stale_assignment_reset` as a stall release (or add an explicit alternative),
  keeping the per-head bounded-retry/attention behaviour in `_pcc_dispatch_stalled`.
- Alternatively/additionally EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh`
  — when the linked issue has an open worker draft checkpoint, emit a release
  reason already in the stall pattern, so continuation stays PR-author bound.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` — add a
  case: unassigned issue, draft PR newer-than-head `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=stale_assignment_reset`
  → continuation dispatched for the PR author; a second stall on the same head
  → one attention record, no loop.

Reference pattern: the existing stall-release cases in
`test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` and `_pcc_dispatch_stalled`.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh`
- Live: after deploy, `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh dispatch-stalled` on an
  unassigned issue whose newest release is `stale_assignment_reset` prints
  `STALE_PR_CONTINUATION` instead of `no current stall release`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`

# Reduce pre-existing Qlty maintainability debt without weakening gates

## What and why

After PR #35361 merged, its changed/new-file Qlty and CodeFactor checks passed, but the repository retains older Qlty smells. The merged-head CI scan for #35361 (Qlty Smell Threshold job in workflow run 39791703553) reported **74 normalized smells** against a threshold of 80: file-complexity 54, similar-code 8, boolean-logic 4, function-parameters 4, function-complexity 3, return-statements 1. The persistent dashboard #24670 is a reporting snapshot (90 at 09:55 UTC), not an actionable implementation brief; use a fresh scan against the latest default branch rather than assuming either count remains current. User requested a separate worker task for *older* findings after #35361 merged; do not reopen or modify the already merged archive migration PR.

Deliver a measured reduction of pre-existing smells in production code with behavior-preserving refactors. Do not raise `QLTY_SMELL_THRESHOLD`, suppress findings, modify Qlty config/CI policy, add exemptions, or trade test coverage and safety guards for a numerical target. Target zero remaining pre-existing smells over successive scoped PRs; if that is too large for one bounded worker run, deliver a coherent reduction in a PR and create deduplicated worker-ready follow-ups for remaining exact files/rules with evidence. Keep this issue open until the remaining scope is addressed, or explicitly record the disposition of every outstanding finding. PRs for partial slices use `For #<this issue>`; only a final verified phase may close it.

## Pre-flight and evidence

- [x] Memory/discovery: prework discovery on 2026-10-22 found no open related PR, two historical commits on sampled files, and merged PR #35361. Recheck ownership/overlapping PRs before editing.
- [x] Existing reporting issue #24670 is persistent and documents that actionable findings belong in separate issues; it is not a duplicate implementation issue.
- [x] Target-path examples were verified by tracked-file discovery; their individual smell counts have not been rechecked. Refresh the SARIF before selecting files.
- [x] Tier: standard — familiar refactor/verification patterns, but scope selection needs judgment; no new security or storage semantics authorized.
- [x] Seed draft PR skipped — no single safe edit is implied by a repository-wide scan, and baseline may change before worker dispatch.

## Files and reference patterns

Start with the latest CI SARIF (`qlty smells --all` with the pinned project CLI if locally available) and select pre-existing findings only. Candidate tracked paths to inspect include `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_budget.py`, `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/openai-provider-auth.mjs`, `.agents/scripts/frontier-harness-run.mjs`, `.agents/scripts/profile-contribution-chart.py`, and `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-webhook-server.py`; their inclusion in the current Qlty report is **not yet established**. Discover the actual affected paths/rules from a fresh scan, not these examples. Avoid touching code refactored by #35361 unless a *current* baseline finding remains.

Reference pattern: #35361 split retry diagnostics/identity and canonical lifecycle test cases into focused modules, preserving the exact runtime contracts. Prefer narrow extractions in high-count files rather than hiding complexity through wrapper-only indirection; maintain API boundaries, Bash compatibility where relevant, and existing private-data protections. Add tests only for uncertain changed behavior or existing repository requirements, not a new test runner.

## Execution and acceptance

1. Fresh baseline: capture HEAD SHA, pinned Qlty version, total and per-rule/per-file counts; record the baseline in the PR body. Check latest open PRs touching selected files. Use linked worktree and normal git safety hooks.
2. Choose a coherent, bounded group of pre-existing findings. Inspect callers and public exports before editing; preserve behavior, error handling, observability, permissions and edge cases. Do not alter unrelated files to manipulate totals.
3. title: Bug: external-author gate transient metadata failure is classified as unclassified_signal
body:
## Observed

During a supervisor pulse on 2026-10-22 (~14:10 UTC), three candidates in a managed repo were skipped with:

```
[dispatch_with_dedup] GH#31404: metadata fetch failed for #<N> in <owner/repo>; skipping dispatch without changing labels (transient)
[pulse-wrapper] Dispatch_max: dispatch_with_dedup returned rc=1 for #<N> ...
[pulse-wrapper] Dispatch_max: #<N> (<owner/repo>) pre-launch failure stage=dispatch_with_dedup rc=1 reason=unclassified_signal
```

The same cycle then logged `Dispatch_max: attempt-recency rotation — 8 candidate(s) attempted without launch ... ordered after the rest of their priority tier` (GH#34363). The current pulse.log has 7 such `GH#31404: metadata fetch failed` lines, each producing `reason=unclassified_signal`.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-commit-gates.sh:230` (external-author gate, `metadata_valid -eq 0` branch) writes only the free-text GH#31404 line. In `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-commit-gates.sh`, right after the existing GH#31404 log line in the `metadata_valid -eq 0` branch, also write:

```
echo "[dispatch_with_dedup] DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=issue_metadata_unavailable signal=transient issue=#${issue_number} repo=${repo_slug}" >>"$LOGFILE"
```

Copy the format from `pulse-dispatch-core.sh:944`. Keep the trust-boundary behaviour (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`): the branch still returns 0 (block) and must not change labels or create a hold.

The existing test `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh` already covers the `issue_metadata_unavailable` marker; no new test is required.

## Task


Make OpenCode DB archiving accept current OpenCode databases whose `project` table has `icon_url_override` in a different column position, by copying rows with explicit column lists instead of positional `SELECT *`.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make OpenCode DB archiving accept current OpenCode databases whose `project` table has `icon_url_override` in a different column position, by copying rows with explicit column lists instead of positional `SELECT *`.

## Why

Runtime evidence (GH#35413 verification, 2026-10-22): `.backup` copies of real isolated DBs created by newer OpenCode builds fail archive with:

`Unsupported or unavailable OpenCode session schema: table=project actual_columns=[id,worktree,vcs,name,icon_url,icon_url_override,icon_color,...] ... reason=column-mismatch; active data was left untouched.`

`opencode_archive_table_schema_supported` (`.agents/scripts/opencode-db-safety-lib.sh:162`) compares ordered column lists, which is correct today because copies are positional (`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO archive.<table> SELECT * FROM <table>`, `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh` around lines 1119-1124 and the copy SQL block near line 1170). Any DB created with the newer column order is therefore never archivable and grows without bound; `maintenance-window` and `auto` report it as a failed archive step every run. Older DBs (where `icon_url_override` was appended by migration) still pass.

## How

- Copy statements: build explicit `INSERT INTO archive.t (cols) SELECT cols FROM t` lists from the supported column set for each table (the archive schema owns the canonical order), so source column order no longer matters.
- Schema check: compare column *sets* (order-insensitive) against the supported generations once copies are name-based; keep fail-closed for unknown/missing columns.
- Reference pattern: `_archive_migrate_schema_columns` in `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh` already reasons per column name.

title: t18760: Release snapshot/provenance reads: configurable retry budget for GitHub empty-body 500s
body:
## Task


Make release snapshot/provenance GitHub reads survive GitHub's intermittent empty-body HTTP 500s by raising the bounded retry budget (configurable attempts, growing backoff) for transport-only failures.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make release snapshot/provenance GitHub reads survive GitHub's intermittent empty-body HTTP 500s by raising the bounded retry budget (configurable attempts, growing backoff) for transport-only failures.

## Why

Observed 2026-10-22 while releasing PR #35417: `aidevops release patch 35417` failed twice in `release-run-capture-authorization` with

`release-snapshot: pull requests for commit 765ef5c376e38f7e91f8a29ead5332a96384b28d in marcusquinn/aidevops: JSON decode error after 3 attempts`

Root cause: `GET repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/pulls` intermittently returns `HTTP/2.0 500` with `Content-Length: 0` (verified with `gh api -i`; sampled 3 of 6 calls at 5s spacing were 500). `gh` 2.103.0 reports only `unexpected end of JSON input` on stderr (no `HTTP 500` text), which the helper correctly classifies as retryable, but `_release_snapshot_gh_read` (`.agents/scripts/release-snapshot-helper.sh:12`) and `_release_provenance_read_json` (`.agents/scripts/release-provenance-helper.sh:70`) hard-code 3 attempts with 1s/2s sleeps. A snapshot reads one endpoint per first-parent commit (13 commits since v3.39.56), so at ~50% per-call failure the whole capture succeeds only ~18% of the time. Each failure leaves the lane `reserved`, which then needs the 5-minute stale-reservation recovery before retrying.

## How

- Add `RELEASE_SNAPSHOT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (default 6, validated positive integer, sane cap e.g. 10) used by both readers; keep auth/404/permission/shape failures non-retryable on the first attempt.
- Backoff: `attempt * RELEASE_SNAPSHOT_RETRY_UNIT` (default unit 2s) so the default budget waits ~30s total; the provenance reader should honour the same unit instead of its literal `sleep "$attempt"`.
- Messages: report `after N attempts` from the variable, not literal 3.
- Reference pattern: existing classifier/retry loop in both functions; keep it, only parameterise.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/release-snapshot-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/release-provenance-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-release-snapshot-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-release-provenance-helper.sh`

## Acceptance

- Transient decode/5xx/empty failures retry up to the configured budget; auth (HTTP 403) still fails after 1 call.
- Existing test assertions updated for the new default (`always` → default attempt count) and still pass with `RELEASE_SNAPSHOT_RETRY_UNIT=0`.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on both helpers.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-release-snapshot-helper.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-release-provenance-helper.sh`.
- Runtime: `aidevops release status <PR>` / a real snapshot capture succeeds while the endpoint is flaky (sample with `gh api -i repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/pulls`).

</details>

<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

</details>

title: repos migrate-layout misreports missing PyYAML as 'Malformed Tabby config'
body:
## What

`aidevops repos migrate-layout plan` fails with `repo layout migration refused: Malformed Tabby config: ~/Library/Application Support/tabby/config.yaml` even though the Tabby config is valid. The real cause is a missing PyYAML import.

## Evidence

- `.agents/scripts/repo-layout-migrate-helper.sh:52` runs the engine with bare `python3`. On macOS with Homebrew this resolves to `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3` (3.15), which has no PyYAML.
- `.agents/scripts/repo_layout_migrate.py:494-504` (`tabby_consumer`) calls `load_tabby_module(...)` **inside** the `try`. Then `tabby-profile-sync.py` → `tabby_appearance_css.py:22 import yaml` raises `ModuleNotFoundError`, and `except Exception` reports it as "Malformed Tabby config".
- The same config parses with `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/python-env/tabby/bin/python3` (the isolated env bootstrapped by `tabby-helper.sh`) and with `/usr/bin/python3` (has user-site PyYAML). Both print `OK: parser accepts config`.

## Fix

1. `repo-layout-migrate-helper.sh`: choose the interpreter the way `tabby-helper.sh` does in `_tabby_python` / `_ensure_tabby_python` (lines 73-119). Prefer `${AIDEVOPS_TABBY_PYTHON_ENV:-~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/python-env/tabby}/bin/python3` when it can import yaml. Otherwise use `python3` if it can import yaml. Otherwise bootstrap the env, or fail clearly when a Tabby config exists. A small shared function is better than copying the code.
2. `repo_layout_migrate.py` `tabby_consumer` (and `prepare_tabby` ~line 1289): load the module outside the parse `try`. Raise a distinct `MigrationError` such as "Tabby validation requires PyYAML (run `aidevops tabby sync` to bootstrap)" for `ImportError`. Keep "Malformed Tabby config" for real parse failures only.

## Verification

- With Homebrew `python3` (no yaml) first on PATH, `aidevops repos migrate-layout plan --workspace ~/Git --source <repo> --output <tmp>/plan.json` no longer reports "Malformed Tabby config". It either succeeds through the isolated env or prints the PyYAML guidance.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tabby-profile-sync.sh` and any existing repo-layout migration tests still pass; `shellcheck` is clean on the helper.

Workaround meanwhile: put `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/python-env/tabby/bin` first on `PATH` before you run `aidevops repos migrate-layout`.

title: worktree-helper.sh remove crashes on macOS: os.listxattr missing in worktree_recovery_retirement_transaction.py
body:
## What happens

`worktree-helper.sh remove <path>` on macOS writes the recovery archive, then stops with a traceback, and the worktree stays in place:

```
File ".agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_retirement_transaction.py", line 43, in inventory
    require(not os.listxattr(path, follow_symlinks=False), "retirement:unsupported-metadata")
AttributeError: module 'os' has no attribute 'listxattr'
Cleanup stopped: the source remains protected and its recoverable archive was retained.
```

Seen with aidevops 3.39.57 and Python 3.15.0 on macOS (Darwin), removing a clean linked worktree with no uncommitted files.

## Cause

Python's `os.listxattr` exists only on Linux, so it is missing on macOS. `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_filesystem.py:28` checks for this (`if not hasattr(os, "listxattr")`) and fails closed with a clear message. `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_retirement_transaction.py:43` (`inventory()`) calls `os.listxattr` without that check, so on macOS every guarded removal that reaches `RestorationProof` → `fingerprint()` → `inventory()` crashes.

`worktree_archive_filesystem.py:32,48,86` also call it. They are behind the `hasattr` guard, so on macOS archiving fails closed before it starts. Check whether the archive path in this run used another route, because the archive was written.

## Fix

- Read extended attributes in a way that works on Linux and macOS (for example a small `list_xattrs(path)` helper: `os.listxattr` where present, otherwise `xattr -l`/`ctypes` `listxattr(2)` with `XATTR_NOFOLLOW`), and use it in both files.
- macOS adds `com.apple.provenance` (and sometimes `com.apple.quarantine`) to many files. Decide whether these block retirement; if every file under a checkout has `com.apple.provenance`, treating any attribute as "unsupported metadata" blocks every removal on a Mac. An allowlist of Apple bookkeeping attributes is probably needed.
- If attributes can't be read on a platform, fail with a `require(...)` code like `retirement:metadata-inspection-unavailable`, not a traceback.

## Verify

- On macOS: `worktree-helper.sh add test/xattr`, then `worktree-helper.sh remove <that path>` removes it and keeps its recovery archive.
- On Linux: the same, and a file with a user xattr still blocks retirement with `retirement:unsupported-metadata`.
- Existing tests for the worktree recovery scripts pass (`rg -l worktree_recovery .agents/scripts/tests`).

### Files Scope
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_filesystem.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_xattrs.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_retirement_transaction.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/worktree_archive_metadata_cases.py`

Implementation evidence: main fdecc6bb7 still uses os.listxattr directly in retirement. Use a shared xattr module for Linux and Darwin no-follow metadata inspection. Allow only Darwin provenance bookkeeping; quarantine and unknown attributes remain blocking. Verify with the existing archive lifecycle suite and simulated Darwin libc calls on this Linux/Python 3.13 runner; native macOS verification needs a macOS runner.

Integration scope recovery: PR #35460 at 9ccf8faf5 adds one `qlty:file-complexity` smell in worktree_archive_filesystem.py (Actions run 39854460156). Move the unchanged reader into worktree_archive_xattrs.py and import it from both consumers, updating existing tests to patch its backend. Ownership remains this assigned worker; collision discovery found no competing target commits/PRs. No behavior, permission or security boundary expansion. Verify the four focused metadata tests, existing archive lifecycle suite, Python annotation compatibility and CI regression gates.

title: tool maintenance: OpenCode npm upgrade lands in a different prefix than the shim target
body:
## Problem

`aidevops update` tool maintenance upgrades OpenCode into a different npm prefix than the one the aidevops shim executes, so the upgrade never takes effect:

```
Running: ... npm install -g opencode-ai@latest
changed 3 packages in 6s
  ⊘ Package 1.19.4 installed, but CLI reports 1.18.34; check binary ownership
```

Observed on a Linux host (v3.39.57):

| Path | Origin | Version |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.local/bin/opencode` | aidevops v1 shim, `exec "/usr/bin/opencode"` | — |
| `/usr/bin/opencode` → `/usr/lib/node_modules/opencode-ai/...` | root-owned system npm prefix | 1.18.34 |
| `~/.nvm/versions/node/<v>/bin/opencode` | user npm prefix (`npm prefix -g`) | 1.19.4 |

## Reproducer

1. Linux host with a root-owned system npm install of `opencode-ai` (`/usr/bin/opencode`) and nvm active for the user (`npm prefix -g` → `~/.nvm/versions/node/<v>`).
2. aidevops setup creates `~/.local/bin/opencode` shim with `exec "/usr/bin/opencode" "$@"`.
3. Run `aidevops update` while a newer `opencode-ai` exists.
4. Observe `⊘ Package <new> installed, but CLI reports <old>`; `/usr/bin/opencode --version` = old, `~/.nvm/.../bin/opencode --version` = new. Repeats on every update.

## Root cause

1. `aidevops_opencode_owner_payload` (`.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh:288-318`) follows the shim to `/usr/bin/opencode` and classifies the owner only as `npm`, without checking which npm prefix owns that binary.
2. The upgrade runs plain `npm install -g`, which writes to the *current* `npm prefix -g` (nvm), not `/usr`.
3. `_setup_ensure_opencode_stable_shim` (`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh:1136+`, lines 1153-1160) keeps the existing valid shim target, so re-running setup never re-points the shim at the newly installed binary.

Result: the version check reports the update every run, the shim (and Pulse via `OPENCODE_BIN`) stay on the old version indefinitely.

## Expected

Either (preferred) the updater detects that the resolved binary's real path is outside `$(npm prefix -g)` and, when the user-prefix install validates, re-points the managed shim to it; or it installs with `--prefix` matching the binary's owner prefix when writable, and otherwise reports a precise actionable message (root-owned prefix, exact command) instead of the generic "check binary ownership".

## Workaround applied locally

Manually changed the shim `exec` target to the nvm binary; `~/.local/bin/opencode --version` → 1.19.4.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tool-version-check.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-opencode.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-install-opencode.sh`

## Verification

- Fixture: shim → system-prefix binary (old version), `npm prefix -g` → user prefix. After tool maintenance the shim resolves to a binary reporting the installed package version, or a precise prefix-mismatch message is printed.
- Existing: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-opencode.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-install-opencode.sh` pass; ShellCheck clean.

title: fix: restored Tabby tabs vanish when their OpenCode database was cleanly closed (sqlite3 -readonly WAL)
body:
## Problem

After quitting and restarting Tabby, clicking a restored OpenCode tab makes the tab disappear instead of resuming its saved session.

## Root cause (verified)

- Restored tabs run `exec aidevops opencode --tabby-shell` with the recovery-marker directory as cwd.
- `session-recovery-data.mjs::querySessionDirectory` validates the session with `sqlite3 -readonly <db>`.
- When OpenCode exits cleanly, as it does when Tabby quits, it checkpoints the WAL and removes `opencode.db-wal`/`-shm`. A read-only connection cannot create the `-shm` index, so `sqlite3` fails with `unable to open database file (14)`.
- The resolver exits with status 1, `opencode-launcher-helper.sh` returns 1, the `exec`'d process ends, and Tabby removes the tab.
- Live sessions still have WAL files, so they resolve normally. That is why only cold sessions fail.

Evidence: 10 of 12 markers referenced by saved Tabby tabs failed with `Could not validate OpenCode recovery database`. `sqlite3 -readonly` and `?mode=ro` both return error 14. `?immutable=1` returns the expected directory.

## Fix

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-recovery-data.mjs`: if the read-only query fails and no `-wal` file exists, retry with `file:<db>?immutable=1`. With no WAL there is no uncheckpointed data, so this read is safe.
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-launcher-helper.sh`: if Tabby recovery or launch-directory validation fails in `--tabby-shell` mode, print the saved session ID and a resume command, then `exec` a login shell instead of exiting. A failed restore no longer removes the tab.

## Verification

- With the patched resolver, all 10 previously failing real markers resolve (exit 0).
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-launcher-helper.sh`: 32/32 pass.
- `node .agents/scripts/tests/test-session-recovery-marker.mjs`: pass.
- ShellCheck is clean.

## What
